title.zh: 卷三百八十三 列傳第一百四十二 陳俊卿 虞允文 辛次膺
title.en: Volume 383 Biographies 142: Chen Junqing, Yu Yunwen, Xin Ciying
title.raw: 卷三百八十三 列傳第一百四十二 陳俊卿 虞允文 辛次膺 Volume 383 Biographies 142: Chen Junqing, Yu Yunwen, Xin Ciying

sentences.zh: 陳俊卿

translations.literal: Chen Junqing
translations.idiomatic: Chen Junqing

sentences.zh: 陳俊卿，字應求，興化人。

translations.literal: Chen Junqing, styled Yingqiu, was a man of Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Junqing, whose courtesy name was Yingqiu, came from Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 幼莊重，不妄言笑。

translations.literal: In youth he was grave and dignified, and did not speak or laugh lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he was solemn and reserved, never given to idle talk or laughter.

sentences.zh: 父死，執喪如成人。

translations.literal: When his father died, he observed mourning like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he carried out the mourning rites with the gravity of a grown man.

sentences.zh: 紹興八年，登進士第，授泉州觀察推官。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Shaoxing he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed investigative adjutant of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Shaoxing era he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed investigative adjutant in Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 服勤職業，同僚宴集，恒謝不往。

translations.literal: He diligently attended to his duties; when colleagues held banquets he always declined to go.
translations.idiomatic: He applied himself diligently to his office, and whenever his colleagues gathered for feasts he invariably excused himself.

sentences.zh: 一日，郡中失火，守汪藻走視之，諸掾屬方飲某所，俊卿輿卒亦假之行，於是例以後至被詰，俊卿唯唯稱謝。

translations.literal: One day a fire broke out in the prefecture. The prefect Wang Zao went to inspect it. The various clerks were drinking at a certain place, and Junqing had also borrowed a carriage and attendants to go there. Accordingly, by rule, those who arrived late were questioned, and Junqing repeatedly bowed and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: One day a fire broke out in the prefecture. Prefect Wang Zao rushed to the scene while his subordinates were drinking at a certain house; Junqing had also borrowed a carriage and runners to join them. By regulation, latecomers were called to account, and Junqing bowed repeatedly and accepted the blame.

sentences.zh: 已而知其實，問故，俊卿曰：「某不能止同僚之行，又資其僕，安得為無過。

translations.literal: Later, when the truth was known, he was asked why. Junqing said, "I could not stop my colleagues from going, and I also made use of their servants—how could I be without fault?
translations.idiomatic: When the facts came out, Wang asked why he had done so. Junqing replied, "I could not stop my colleagues from going, and I even used their servants on the way—how could I claim to be blameless?

sentences.zh: 時公方盛怒，其忍幸自解，重人之罪乎？」

translations.literal: At that time Your Excellency was in great anger—how could I bear to save myself by chance and increase another's guilt?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Excellency was furious at the time; how could I seek to clear myself and heap the blame on others?"

sentences.zh: 藻歎服，以為不可及。

translations.literal: Wang Zao sighed in admiration and considered him beyond compare.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zao sighed in admiration and concluded that Junqing was beyond compare.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，秦檜當國，察其不附己，以為南外睦宗院教授。

translations.literal: When his term expired, Qin Hui held power, saw that he did not attach himself to him, and made him professor at the Southern Outer Muzong Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, Qin Hui was in power; perceiving that Junqing would not align with him, he assigned him to teach at the Southern Outer Muzong Academy.

sentences.zh: 尋添通判南劍州，未上而檜死，乃以校書郎召。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed vice-prefect of Nanjian, but before he took up the post Qin Hui died, and he was summoned as collator.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given an additional appointment as vice-prefect of Nanjian, but before he could take up the post Qin Hui died, and he was recalled to the capital as collator.

sentences.zh: 孝宗時為普安郡王，高宗命擇端厚靜重者輔導之，除著作佐郎兼王府教授。

translations.literal: At that time Xiaozong was Prince of Pu'an. Gaozong ordered that upright, generous, calm, and weighty men be chosen to instruct him, and Junqing was appointed assistant compiler and concurrently professor in the princely household.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong was then Prince of Pu'an. Gaozong ordered that upright, steady men of substance be chosen to guide him, and Junqing was made assistant compiler and concurrently tutor in the princely household.

sentences.zh: 講經輒寓規戒，正色特立。

translations.literal: Whenever he lectured on the classics he would embed admonitions; with stern countenance he stood apart.
translations.idiomatic: In his lectures he always wove in admonitions, maintaining a grave bearing and holding himself apart.

sentences.zh: 王好鞠戲，因誦韓愈諫張建封書以諷，王敬納之。

translations.literal: The prince loved cuju ball games. Junqing therefore recited Han Yu's memorial admonishing Zhang Jianfeng as an indirect remonstrance, and the prince respectfully accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was fond of cuju. Junqing recited Han Yu's memorial admonishing Zhang Jianfeng as an oblique warning, and the prince received the lesson with respect.

sentences.zh: 累遷監察御史、殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to investigating censor and palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to investigating censor and then palace censor.

sentences.zh: 首言：「人主以兼聽為美，必本至公；

translations.literal: He first said: "For a ruler, to hear many sides is beautiful, but it must be rooted in utmost fairness;
translations.idiomatic: In his first memorial he wrote: "A ruler does well to hear many voices, but only when he is grounded in perfect fairness;

sentences.zh: 人臣以不欺為忠，必達大體。

translations.literal: for a minister, not to deceive is loyalty, but he must grasp the larger pattern.
translations.idiomatic: for a minister, loyalty lies in refusing to deceive, yet he must also grasp the larger design of state.

sentences.zh: 御下之道，恩威並施，抑驕將，作士氣，則紀綱正而號令行矣。」

translations.literal: The way to govern subordinates is to apply both kindness and awe, restrain arrogant generals, and rouse the spirit of the troops—then discipline will be correct and orders will be carried out."
translations.idiomatic: To command subordinates, kindness and severity must go together: curb arrogant generals and lift the morale of the ranks, and discipline will stand straight while orders are obeyed."

sentences.zh: 遂劾韓仲通本以獄事附檜，冤陷無辜，檜黨盡逐而仲通獨全；

translations.literal: He then impeached Han Zhongtong, who had originally attached himself to Qin Hui through prison cases and wrongfully trapped the innocent; Qin's faction had all been driven out while Zhongtong alone survived;
translations.idiomatic: He then impeached Han Zhongtong, who had curried favor with Qin Hui through prison cases and wrongfully ruined innocent men; Qin's faction had been swept away while Zhongtong alone remained untouched;

sentences.zh: 劉寶總戎京口，恣掊克，且拒命不分戍；

translations.literal: and Liu Bao, commanding troops at Jingkou, wantonly extorted and moreover disobeyed orders by refusing to distribute garrison duties;
translations.idiomatic: and Liu Bao, who commanded the forces at Jingkou, extorted his men at will and defied orders by refusing to rotate garrison duty;

sentences.zh: 二人遂抵罪。

translations.literal: the two men were thereupon punished.
translations.idiomatic: both men were punished accordingly.

sentences.zh: 湯思退專政，俊卿曰：「冬日無雲而雷，宰相上不當天心，下不厭人望。」

translations.literal: When Tang Situi monopolized government, Junqing said: "Winter days without clouds yet with thunder—the chief minister is not attuned to Heaven's mind above and does not satisfy people's hopes below."
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Situi dominated the government, Junqing said: "Thunder in a cloudless winter sky—such a chief minister fails Heaven above and the people below."

sentences.zh: 詔罷思退。

translations.literal: An edict dismissed Situi.
translations.idiomatic: An edict removed Situi from office.

sentences.zh: 時災異數見，金人侵軼之勢已形。

translations.literal: At that time portents and anomalies appeared repeatedly, and the Jin people's tendency to raid and harass had already taken shape.
translations.idiomatic: Omens and disasters multiplied, and Jin raids were already taking shape along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 俊卿乃疏言：「張浚忠藎，白首不渝，竊聞讒言其陰有異志。

translations.literal: Junqing then memorialized: "Zhang Jun is loyal to the marrow; white-haired, he has never wavered. I have privately heard slander that he secretly harbors a different intent.
translations.idiomatic: Junqing memorialized: "Zhang Jun has been loyal to the bone; in old age he has not wavered. Yet I hear whispers that he secretly harbors disloyal designs.

sentences.zh: 夫浚之得人心、伏士論，為其忠義有素。

translations.literal: That Jun wins people's hearts and commands the respect of scholar-official opinion is because his loyalty and righteousness have long been established.
translations.idiomatic: He wins men's hearts and commands the respect of the literati precisely because his loyalty has been proven over many years.

sentences.zh: 反是，則人將去之，誰復與為變乎？」

translations.literal: Were it otherwise, people would abandon him—who would join him in rebellion?"
translations.idiomatic: Were it otherwise, men would desert him—who would follow him in treason?"

sentences.zh: 疏入，未報，因請對，力言之，上始悟。

translations.literal: The memorial entered but received no reply. He therefore requested an audience and spoke forcefully; the emperor then understood.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went in without reply; he sought an audience and spoke forcefully until the emperor understood.

sentences.zh: 數月，以浚守建康。

translations.literal: Several months later, Jun was made defender of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: A few months later Zhang Jun was appointed to defend Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 又言：「內侍張去為陰沮用兵，且陳避敵計，搖成算，請按軍法。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The inner attendant Zhang Quwei secretly obstructs the use of troops and moreover proposes plans to avoid the enemy, shaking settled strategy—please punish him according to military law."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged: "The eunuch Zhang Quwei secretly undermines the war effort and urges plans to avoid the enemy, unsettling our strategy—he should be punished under military law."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿可謂仁者之勇。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You may be called the courage of the benevolent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You have the courage of a true gentleman."

sentences.zh: 除權兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed acting vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: Junqing was appointed acting vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 金主亮渡淮，俊卿受詔整浙西水軍，李寶因之遂有膠西之捷。

translations.literal: When the Jin ruler Hailing crossed the Huai, Junqing received orders to reorganize the Zhexi naval forces; Li Bao thereby achieved the victory at Jiaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin emperor Hailing crossed the Huai, Junqing was ordered to reorganize the naval forces of western Zhejiang; Li Bao, acting under his authority, won the victory at Jiaoxi.

sentences.zh: 亮死，詔俊卿治淮東堡砦屯田，所過安輯流亡。

translations.literal: When Hailing died, an edict ordered Junqing to administer fortresses, stockades, and garrison farms east of the Huai; wherever he passed he settled and comforted displaced people.
translations.idiomatic: After Hailing's death, Junqing was ordered to oversee fortresses and garrison farms east of the Huai, settling refugees wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 金主褒新立，申舊好，廷臣多附和議。

translations.literal: The new Jin ruler Bao had just ascended and renewed the old friendship; many court officials echoed the peace faction.
translations.idiomatic: The new Jin ruler Bao had just taken the throne and proposed renewing friendly relations; many at court favored peace.

sentences.zh: 俊卿奏：「和戎本非得已，若以得故疆為實利，得之未必能守，是亦虛文而已。

translations.literal: Junqing memorialized: "Making peace with the barbarians was originally not what we wished; if recovering the old territory is taken as real profit, gaining it does not necessarily mean we can hold it—that too is empty formality.
translations.idiomatic: Junqing argued: "Peace with the Jin was never our first choice; even if recovering lost territory were a real gain, we might not be able to hold it—such talk is empty form.

sentences.zh: 今不若先正名，名正則國威強，歲幣可損。」

translations.literal: Now it would be better first to rectify names; when names are correct national prestige is strong and annual tribute can be reduced."
translations.idiomatic: We should first set our diplomatic standing straight; once our position is clear our prestige will rise and the annual tribute can be cut."

sentences.zh: 因陳選將練兵、屯田減租之策，擇文臣有膽略者為參佐，俾察軍政、習戎務以儲將材。

translations.literal: He then set forth policies of selecting generals, training troops, garrison farming, and reducing rents; he chose civil officials of courage and strategy as aides so they might inspect military administration, study military affairs, and store up talent for command.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed selecting good generals, training troops, garrison farming, and rent relief; civil officials of courage and judgment should serve as aides, inspecting military affairs and learning the art of war to build a pool of future commanders.

sentences.zh: 孝宗受禪，言：「為國之要有三：用人、賞功、罰罪，所以行之者至公而已，願留聖意。」

translations.literal: When Xiaozong received the abdication, he said: "The essentials of governing a state are three: employing men, rewarding merit, and punishing crime—the means to carry these out is nothing but utmost fairness; I beg Your Majesty to keep this in mind."
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong ascended the throne, Junqing wrote: "Three things are essential to governing a state: appointing the right men, rewarding merit, and punishing crime—and all three depend on perfect fairness. I beg Your Majesty to keep this in mind."

sentences.zh: 遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to drafter of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to drafter of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時孝宗志在興復，方以閫外事屬張浚。

translations.literal: At that time Xiaozong's aim was restoration, and he had just entrusted frontier affairs to Zhang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong was bent on recovery and had just entrusted frontier affairs to Zhang Jun.

sentences.zh: 以俊卿忠義，沉靖有謀，以本職充江淮宣撫判官兼權建康府事。

translations.literal: Because Junqing was loyal and righteous, calm and weighty, and resourceful, he was made, in his existing rank, judicial commissioner of the Jiang-Huai pacification commission and concurrently acting prefect of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Because Junqing was loyal, steady, and shrewd, he was made judicial commissioner on the Jiang-Huai pacification commission and concurrently acting prefect of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 奏曰：「吳璘得孤軍深入，敵悉眾拒戰，久不決，危道也。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Wu Lin has led an isolated army deep in; the enemy has mustered all forces to resist, and the outcome has long been undecided—this is a perilous course.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Wu Lin has pushed deep with a lone army while the enemy masses every man to resist him; the campaign drags on unresolved—a dangerous course.

sentences.zh: 兩淮事勢已急，盍分遣舟師直搗山東，彼必還師自救，而璘得乘勝定關中。

translations.literal: The situation on both sides of the Huai is already urgent. Why not dispatch naval forces separately to strike straight at Shandong? They will surely withdraw troops to save themselves, and Lin can seize the victory to settle Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai front is already critical. Send a fleet to strike Shandong directly; the Jin will have to recall their armies, and Lin can then press his advantage and secure Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 我及其未至，潰其腹心，此不世之功也。」

translations.literal: Before they arrive, we can break their heartland—this would be an achievement for the ages."
translations.idiomatic: Strike their heartland before they can respond, and the victory would be one for the ages."

sentences.zh: 會主和議方堅，詔璘班師，亦召俊卿。

translations.literal: Just then the peace faction was firm; an edict ordered Lin to withdraw, and Junqing was also recalled.
translations.idiomatic: But the peace party was ascendant; an edict recalled Lin and summoned Junqing back as well.

sentences.zh: 奏陳十事：定規模，振紀綱，勵風俗，明賞罰，重名器，遵祖宗之法，蠲無名之賦。

translations.literal: He memorialized ten matters: fixing the scale of government, reviving discipline, encouraging customs, clarifying rewards and punishments, honoring titles and offices, following ancestral law, and remitting irregular levies.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted ten proposals: set the scale of government, restore discipline, encourage proper conduct, clarify rewards and punishments, honor rank and office, follow ancestral law, and abolish irregular levies.

sentences.zh: 隆興初元，建都督府，俊卿除禮部侍郎參贊軍事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing a supreme command was established; Junqing was made vice minister of rites to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longxing a supreme command was established, and Junqing was made vice minister of rites to assist in military planning.

sentences.zh: 張浚初謀大舉北伐，俊卿以為未可。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun at first planned a great northern expedition; Junqing thought it not yet feasible.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun at first planned a major northern campaign, but Junqing judged the time not ripe.

sentences.zh: 會諜報敵聚糧邊地，諸將以為秋必至，宜先其未動舉兵，浚乃請於朝出師。

translations.literal: Then spies reported the enemy gathering grain on the frontier; the generals thought they would surely come in autumn and that troops should be moved before the enemy acted. Jun thereupon requested permission from court to take the field.
translations.idiomatic: Spies reported the Jin hoarding grain on the frontier; the generals expected an autumn offensive and urged striking before the enemy moved. Zhang Jun petitioned the court to march.

sentences.zh: 已而邵宏淵果以兵潰，俊卿退保揚州。

translations.literal: Before long Shao Hongyuan's troops indeed collapsed in rout; Junqing withdrew to defend Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Shao Hongyuan's army collapsed in defeat, and Junqing fell back to defend Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 主和議者幸其敗，橫議搖之。

translations.literal: Those who favored peace rejoiced at the defeat and spread reckless talk to shake confidence.
translations.idiomatic: The peace faction welcomed the defeat and spread reckless talk to undermine the war party.

sentences.zh: 浚上疏待罪，俊卿亦乞從坐，詔貶兩秩。

translations.literal: Jun submitted a memorial awaiting punishment; Junqing also asked to share guilt. An edict demoted both two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun submitted a memorial accepting blame; Junqing asked to share the punishment. Both were demoted two ranks by edict.

sentences.zh: 諫臣尹穡附思退，議罷浚都督，改宣撫使治揚州。

translations.literal: The remonstrating official Yin Ji, attached to Situi, proposed abolishing Jun's supreme command and making him pacification commissioner to govern Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Yin Ji, allied with Situi, proposed stripping Zhang Jun of supreme command and making him pacification commissioner at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 俊卿奏：「浚果不可用，別屬賢將；

translations.literal: Junqing memorialized: "If Jun truly cannot be used, assign another worthy general;
translations.idiomatic: Junqing memorialized: "If Zhang Jun truly cannot serve, appoint another able commander;

sentences.zh: 若欲責其後效，降官示罰，古法也。

translations.literal: if you wish to hold him accountable for later results, demoting his rank to show punishment is the ancient way.
translations.idiomatic: if you wish to hold him to account for future results, demotion is the ancient way to show censure.

sentences.zh: 今削都督重權，置揚州死地，如有奏請，臺諫沮之，人情解體，尚何後效之圖？

translations.literal: Now you strip the supreme commander's weighty authority and place him in the dead ground of Yangzhou; if he makes requests, the censorate obstructs them—morale disintegrates—how can there still be hope for later results?
translations.idiomatic: But to strip him of supreme command and post him in the trap of Yangzhou, where every request is blocked by the censors, is to dissolve morale entirely—what hope then of future success?

sentences.zh: 議者但知惡浚而欲殺之，不復為宗社計。

translations.literal: The debaters only know hatred of Jun and wish to destroy him; they no longer plan for the altars of state and grain.
translations.idiomatic: His critics care only to destroy Zhang Jun and no longer think of the dynasty's welfare.

sentences.zh: 願下詔戒中外協濟，使浚自效。」

translations.literal: I beg that an edict warn inside and outside to cooperate, and let Jun prove himself."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to issue an edict calling on all to cooperate and let Zhang Jun redeem himself."

sentences.zh: 疏再上，上悟，即命浚都督，且召為相，卒為思退、穡所擠，遣視師江、淮。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted again the emperor understood; he immediately restored Jun as supreme commander and also summoned him as chief councilor, but in the end Situi and Ji forced him out and sent him to inspect the armies on the Jiang and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: When he submitted again the emperor understood; Zhang Jun was restored to supreme command and summoned as chief councilor, but Situi and Yin Ji eventually forced him out and sent him to inspect the Jiang-Huai front.

sentences.zh: 俊卿累章請罪，以寶文閣待制知泉州，請祠，提舉太平興國宮。

translations.literal: Junqing repeatedly memorialized asking punishment; he was made academician of the Baowen Pavilion and prefect of Quanzhou, requested a sinecure, and was made superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Junqing repeatedly asked to share the blame; he was made academician of the Baowen Pavilion and prefect of Quanzhou, then requested leave and was made superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.

sentences.zh: 思退既竄，太學諸生伏闕下乞召俊卿。

translations.literal: After Situi was banished, students of the Imperial Academy prostrated themselves below the palace gate begging that Junqing be summoned.
translations.idiomatic: After Situi was banished, students of the Imperial Academy knelt at the palace gate petitioning for Junqing's recall.

sentences.zh: 乾道元年，入對，上勞撫之，因極論朋黨之弊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiandao he entered audience; the emperor comforted and encouraged him, and he thereupon spoke at length on the harm of faction.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qiandao he was received in audience; the emperor comforted him warmly, and Junqing spoke at length on the evils of faction.

sentences.zh: 除吏部侍郎、同修國史。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice minister of personnel and co-compiler of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice minister of personnel and co-compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 論人才當以氣節為主，氣節者，小有過當容之；

translations.literal: He argued that in judging talent moral backbone should come first; for those with backbone, minor faults should be tolerated;
translations.idiomatic: He argued that in appointing men moral backbone should come first; men of backbone may be forgiven minor faults;

sentences.zh: 邪佞者，甚有才當察之。

translations.literal: for the wicked and fawning, however talented they may be, one should scrutinize them.
translations.idiomatic: but the wicked and fawning, however talented, must be watched closely.

sentences.zh: 錢端禮起戚里為參政，窺相位甚急，館閣之士上疏斥之。

translations.literal: Qian Duanli rose from the empress's kin to be vice grand councilor and watched the chief ministership very eagerly; scholars of the Hanlin and academies memorialized to denounce him.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Duanli, a relative of the empress, had risen to vice grand councilor and was openly angling for the chief ministership; Hanlin scholars memorialized against him.

sentences.zh: 端禮遣客密告俊卿，己即相，當引共政。

translations.literal: Duanli sent a messenger secretly to tell Junqing that once he himself became chief councilor he would bring Junqing in to share government.
translations.idiomatic: Duanli sent a secret envoy promising that once he became chief councilor he would bring Junqing in as his partner.

sentences.zh: 深拒不聽。

translations.literal: Junqing firmly refused and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Junqing firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 翌日，進讀《寶訓》，適及外戚，因言：「本朝家法，外戚不預政，有深意，陛下宜謹守。」

translations.literal: The next day, while lecturing on the Precious Instructions, he happened upon the section on empress's kin and therefore said: "Our dynasty's household law is that empress's kin do not participate in government—this has deep meaning; Your Majesty should strictly observe it."
translations.idiomatic: The next day, lecturing on the Precious Instructions, he came to the passage on empress's kin and said: "Our dynasty's household law keeps empress's relatives out of government for good reason; Your Majesty should hold to it strictly."

sentences.zh: 上首肯，端禮憾之。

translations.literal: The emperor nodded assent; Duanli resented it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded agreement; Duanli bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 知建康府。

translations.literal: He was made prefect of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 逾年，授吏部尚書。

translations.literal: After a year he was given the post of minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 時上未能屏鞠戲，將游獵白石。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had not yet been able to give up cuju games and was about to go hunting at Baishi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had not yet given up cuju and was planning a hunting excursion at Baishi.

sentences.zh: 俊卿引漢桓靈、唐敬穆及司馬相如之言力以為戒。

translations.literal: Junqing cited the examples of the Han emperors Huan and Ling, Tang Jingzong and Muzong, and the words of Sima Xiangru, urging restraint with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Junqing cited the Han emperors Huan and Ling, Tang Jingzong and Muzong, and Sima Xiangru's admonitions, urging restraint with all his force.

sentences.zh: 上喜曰：「備見忠讜，朕決意用卿矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said with pleasure: "I have fully seen your loyal forthrightness; I am resolved to employ you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said with pleasure, "I have seen your loyal candor; I am resolved to employ you.

sentences.zh: 朕在藩邸，知卿為忠臣。」

translations.literal: When I was in the princely residence I knew you were a loyal minister."
translations.idiomatic: When I was still in the princely residence I knew you were a loyal minister."

sentences.zh: 俊卿拜謝。

translations.literal: Junqing bowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Junqing bowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 受詔館金使，遂拜同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He received orders to host the Jin envoys and was then appointed vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to host the Jin envoys, he was then appointed vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時曾覿、龍大淵怙舊恩，竊威福，士大夫頗出其門。

translations.literal: At that time Zeng Di and Long Dayuan relied on old favor and secretly wielded power and blessings; many scholar-officials came through their doors.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Di and Long Dayuan traded on old favor to wield secret influence, and many officials passed through their doors.

sentences.zh: 及俊卿館伴，大淵副之，公見外，不交一語，大淵納謁，亦謝不接。

translations.literal: When Junqing served as host, Dayuan was his deputy; in public view they exchanged not a single word. Dayuan offered a visit and Junqing likewise declined to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: When Junqing served as chief host with Dayuan as deputy, they exchanged not a word in public; when Dayuan offered a private visit, Junqing declined to receive him.

sentences.zh: 洪邁白俊卿：「人言鄭聞除右史，某當除某官，信乎？」

translations.literal: Hong Mai told Junqing: "People say Zheng Wen is to be made right secretary; I am to be given a certain office—is it true?"
translations.idiomatic: Hong Mai asked Junqing: "People say Zheng Wen is to be made right secretary and I am to receive a certain post—is it true?"

sentences.zh: 詰所從，邁以淵、覿告。

translations.literal: Asked his source, Mai named Dayuan and Di.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed for his source, Mai named Dayuan and Di.

sentences.zh: 具以邁語質於上，上曰：「朕曷嘗謀及此輩，必竊聽得之。」

translations.literal: Junqing reported Mai's words fully to the emperor. The emperor said: "When did I ever consult these people? They must have eavesdropped to learn it."
translations.idiomatic: Junqing reported this fully to the emperor, who said, "I never consulted those men on appointments—they must have been eavesdropping."

sentences.zh: 有旨出淵、覿，中外稱快。

translations.literal: An edict banished Dayuan and Di; inside and outside the court rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: An edict banished Dayuan and Di, to general satisfaction throughout the court.

sentences.zh: 金移文邊吏，取前所俘。

translations.literal: The Jin sent a document to frontier officials demanding return of previously captured persons.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin sent a diplomatic note to frontier officials demanding the return of captives taken earlier.

sentences.zh: 俊卿請報以「誓書云：俘虜叛亡是兩事，俘虜發已多，叛亡不應遣。

translations.literal: Junqing asked that the reply state: "The sworn document says captives and defectors are two different matters; captives have already been sent in great number—defectors should not be returned.
translations.idiomatic: Junqing proposed replying: "The treaty distinguishes captives from defectors; we have already returned many captives, and defectors should not be sent back.

sentences.zh: 且本朝兩淮民，上國俘虜亡慮數萬，本朝未嘗以為言，恐壞和議，使兩境民不安。

translations.literal: Moreover, among the people on both sides of the Huai in our dynasty, and among captives and fugitives of your state, there are surely tens of thousands; our dynasty has never raised the matter, fearing to damage the peace and make the people on both sides uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, tens of thousands of our people on both sides of the Huai and your captives and fugitives remain unsettled; we have never raised the matter, fearing to damage peace and unsettle both peoples.

sentences.zh: 或至交兵，則屈直勝負有在矣。」

translations.literal: If it comes to exchanging blows, then right and wrong and victory and defeat will have their place."
translations.idiomatic: If it comes to war, the merits of each side will be decided on the field."

sentences.zh: 鎮江軍帥戚方刻削軍士，俊卿奏：「內臣中有主方者，當併懲之。」

translations.literal: Qi Fang, military commander at Zhenjiang, harshly squeezed the troops. Junqing memorialized: "Among the inner attendants there are those who back Fang—they should be punished together."
translations.idiomatic: Qi Fang, commander at Zhenjiang, was extorting his troops. Junqing memorialized: "Some eunuchs back Fang; they should be punished as well."

sentences.zh: 即詔罷方，以內侍陳瑤、李宗回付大理究贓狀。

translations.literal: An edict at once dismissed Fang and handed the inner attendants Chen Yao and Li Zonghui to the Court of Judicial Review to investigate their corrupt acts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict immediately dismissed Fang and referred the eunuchs Chen Yao and Li Zonghui to the Court of Judicial Review to investigate corruption.

sentences.zh: 十一月，當郊而雷，上內出手詔，戒飭大臣，葉顒、魏杞坐罷。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, when the suburban sacrifice was due, thunder sounded. The emperor issued a hand edict from within warning and admonishing the great ministers; Ye Yong and Wei Qi were dismissed on account of it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, thunder sounded on the eve of the suburban sacrifice. The emperor issued a personal edict admonishing his ministers; Ye Yong and Wei Qi were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 俊卿參知政事。

translations.literal: Junqing was made vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Junqing was appointed vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 時四明獻銀礦，將召冶工即禁中鍛之。

translations.literal: At that time Siming presented a silver mine; smelters were to be summoned to forge it right in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Siming presented a silver mine, and the court planned to summon smelters to work it inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 俊卿奏：「不務帝王之大，而屑屑有司之細，恐為有識所窺。」

translations.literal: Junqing memorialized: "Not attending to the great affairs of an emperor but fussing over the petty details of clerks—I fear the perceptive will see through this."
translations.idiomatic: Junqing objected: "To neglect the great affairs of empire for the petty work of clerks will be noticed by men of judgment."

sentences.zh: 從官梁克家、莫濟俱求補外，俊卿奏：「二人皆賢，其去可惜。」

translations.literal: Attendants Liang Kejia and Mo Ji both sought posts outside the capital. Junqing memorialized: "Both men are worthy; their departure would be a pity."
translations.idiomatic: Attendants Liang Kejia and Mo Ji both sought provincial posts. Junqing urged: "Both are able men; their loss would be regrettable."

sentences.zh: 於是劾奏洪邁奸險讒佞，不宜在左右，罷之。

translations.literal: He thereupon impeached Hong Mai as treacherous, dangerous, slanderous, and fawning, unfit to be at the emperor's side, and had him removed.
translations.idiomatic: He then impeached Hong Mai as treacherous, slanderous, and unfit to serve at court, and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 減福建鈔鹽，罷江西和糴、廣西折米鹽錢，蠲諸道宿逋金穀錢帛以巨萬計，於是政事稍歸中書矣。

translations.literal: He reduced Fujian's paper-salt levy, abolished Jiangxi's grain-purchase commutation and Guangxi's rice-conversion salt money, and remitted arrears of grain, cash, and silk across circuits amounting to tens of thousands—thereby government affairs gradually returned to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He cut Fujian's salt surcharge, abolished Jiangxi's grain-purchase commutation and Guangxi's rice-conversion levy, and remitted arrears across the circuits totaling tens of millions—so that government gradually returned to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 龍大淵死，上憐曾覿，欲召之。

translations.literal: When Long Dayuan died, the emperor pitied Zeng Di and wished to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: After Long Dayuan died, the emperor took pity on Zeng Di and wished to recall him.

sentences.zh: 俊卿曰：「自出此兩人，中外莫不稱頌。

translations.literal: Junqing said: "Since these two men were removed, inside and outside the court have none but praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Junqing said, "Since those two men were banished, the whole court has applauded the decision.

sentences.zh: 今復召，必大失天下望。

translations.literal: To summon them back now would greatly disappoint the world's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: To recall them now would deeply disappoint the empire.

sentences.zh: 臣請先罷。」

translations.literal: Your servant asks to resign first."
translations.idiomatic: I beg to resign first."

sentences.zh: 遂不召。

translations.literal: Di was therefore not summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Di was not recalled.

sentences.zh: 殿前指揮使王琪被旨按視兩淮城壁還，薦和州教授劉甄夫，得召。

translations.literal: Wang Qi, commander of the Palace Front, having been ordered to inspect the walls on both sides of the Huai and returned, recommended Liu Zhenfu, professor of Hezhou, who was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qi, commander of the Palace Front, returned from inspecting the Huai fortifications and recommended Liu Zhenfu, professor of Hezhou, who was summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 俊卿言：「琪薦兵將官乃其職，教官有才，何預琪事。」

translations.literal: Junqing said: "For Qi to recommend military officers is his duty; if an instructor has talent, what has that to do with Qi?"
translations.idiomatic: Junqing objected: "Qi may recommend military officers—that is his duty—but a talented instructor is none of his business."

sentences.zh: 會揚州奏琪傳旨增築城已訖事，俊卿請於上，未嘗有是命。

translations.literal: Just then Yangzhou reported that Qi had transmitted an order to enlarge the city walls and that the work was finished. Junqing asked the emperor, who said no such command had ever been issued.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Yangzhou reported that Qi had claimed an imperial order to enlarge the city walls and that the work was done. Junqing asked the emperor, who said he had issued no such command.

sentences.zh: 俊卿曰：「若詐傳上旨，非小故。」

translations.literal: Junqing said: "If he falsely transmitted the emperor's order, this is no small matter."
translations.idiomatic: Junqing said, "To forge an imperial order is no small offense."

sentences.zh: 奏言：「人主萬幾，豈能盡防閑，所恃者紀綱、號令、賞罰耳。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The ruler faces ten thousand affairs—how can he guard against everything? What he relies on is discipline, orders, and rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "A ruler faces ten thousand affairs and cannot guard against every abuse; he relies on discipline, clear orders, and rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 不誅琪，何所不為。」

translations.literal: If Qi is not punished, what will men not dare to do?"
translations.idiomatic: If Qi goes unpunished, what will men not dare to do?"

sentences.zh: 琪削秩罷官。

translations.literal: Qi was demoted in rank and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was demoted and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 先是，禁中密旨直下諸軍，宰相多不預聞，內官張方事覺，俊卿奏：「自今百司承御筆處分事，須奏審方行。」

translations.literal: Previously, secret orders from within the palace went straight down to the armies, and the chief ministers often did not hear of them beforehand. When the inner attendant Zhang Fang's affair was exposed, Junqing memorialized: "From now on, whenever the hundred offices receive imperial brush orders for disposal, they must report for review before acting."
translations.idiomatic: Previously secret palace orders went straight to the armies without the chief ministers' knowledge. When the eunuch Zhang Fang's misconduct came to light, Junqing proposed, "From now on, whenever the hundred offices receive imperial brush orders for disposal, they must report for review before execution."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 既而以內諸司不樂，收前命。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because the inner palace offices were displeased, the earlier order was withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the inner palace offices objected and the order was rescinded.

sentences.zh: 俊卿言：「張方、王琪事，聖斷已明，忽諭臣曰：『禁中取一飲一食，必待申審，豈不留滯。』

translations.literal: Junqing said: "In the affairs of Zhang Fang and Wang Qi, Your Majesty's judgment was already clear. Suddenly I was told: 'For the palace to take a drink or a meal, it must await review and approval—would that not cause delay?
translations.idiomatic: Junqing said, "Your judgment in the Zhang Fang and Wang Qi cases was already clear. Suddenly I was told, 'Must the palace wait for review even to take food and drink—would that not cause delay?

sentences.zh: 臣所慮者，命令之大，如三衙發兵，戶部取財，豈為宮禁細微事。

translations.literal: What your servant fears are great commands—such as the Three Commands dispatching troops or the Ministry of Revenue taking funds—not petty matters of the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: What I fear are great commands—dispatching troops from the Three Commands, drawing funds from the Ministry of Revenue—not petty palace matters.

sentences.zh: 臣等備數，出內陛下命令耳。

translations.literal: We ministers merely fill our posts and carry out Your Majesty's commands.
translations.idiomatic: We ministers merely fill our posts and carry out Your Majesty's orders.

sentences.zh: 凡奏審欲取決陛下，非臣欲專之，且非新條，申舊制耳。

translations.literal: Reporting for review is to let Your Majesty decide—it is not that your servant wishes to monopolize authority, and it is no new regulation but simply restoring the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Review is meant to let Your Majesty decide—not to monopolize power, and this is no innovation but the restoration of old practice.

sentences.zh: 已行復收，中外惶惑，恐小人以疑似激聖怒。」

translations.literal: What was already enacted has been withdrawn; inside and outside the court are alarmed and confused, fearing petty men may stir Your Majesty's anger with suspicions."
translations.idiomatic: To enact a rule and then withdraw it alarms the court, and I fear petty men may stir Your Majesty's anger with suspicions."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕豈以小人言疑卿等耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Would I suspect you because of petty men's words?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Would I suspect you because of petty men's words?"

sentences.zh: 同知樞密院事劉珙進對，爭辨激切，忤旨，既退，手詔除珙端明殿學士，奉外祠。

translations.literal: Liu Gong, vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, entered audience and argued so vehemently that he offended the emperor. After he withdrew, a hand edict made Gong academician of the Duanming Hall and assigned him an outside sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gong, vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, argued so fiercely in audience that he offended the emperor. After he withdrew, a personal edict made him academician of the Duanming Hall and sent him to an outside sinecure.

sentences.zh: 俊卿即藏去，密具奏：「前日奏劄，臣實草定，以為有罪，臣當先罷。

translations.literal: Junqing at once concealed the edict and secretly memorialized in full: "The memorial of the other day was in fact drafted by your servant. If there is guilt, your servant should resign first.
translations.idiomatic: Junqing hid the edict and secretly memorialized: "I drafted the memorial in question. If anyone is at fault, I should resign first.

sentences.zh: 珙之除命，未敢奉詔。

translations.literal: Gong's appointment order—I dare not accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not accept the edict appointing Gong.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位以來，納諫諍，體大臣，皆盛德事。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, accepting remonstrance and treating great ministers with consideration have all been deeds of surpassing virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty's accession, accepting remonstrance and treating great ministers with respect have been marks of surpassing virtue.

sentences.zh: 今珙以小事獲罪，臣恐自此大臣皆阿順持祿，非國家福。」

translations.literal: Now Gong is punished for a small matter; your servant fears that from this onward great ministers will all flatter and hold their salaries—this is no blessing to the state."
translations.idiomatic: To punish Gong for a small matter—I fear great ministers will henceforth flatter and cling to their salaries, which is no blessing to the state."

sentences.zh: 上色悔久之，命珙帥江西。

translations.literal: The emperor's expression showed regret for a long time; he ordered Gong to command Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed long regret and appointed Gong to command Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 俊卿退自劾，上手劄留之，且曰：「卿雖百請，朕必不從。」

translations.literal: Junqing withdrew and impeached himself. The emperor sent a hand note to keep him, saying: "Even if you request a hundred times, I will not consent."
translations.idiomatic: Junqing withdrew and submitted his resignation. The emperor sent a personal note refusing it: "Even if you ask a hundred times, I will not agree."

sentences.zh: 四年十月，制授尚書右僕射、同中書門下平章事兼樞密使。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year he was appointed by decree right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, joint manager of affairs with the Secretariat and Chancellery, and concurrently commissioner of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year he was appointed right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, grand councilor, and concurrently commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 俊卿以用人為己任，所除吏皆一時選，獎廉退，抑奔競。

translations.literal: Junqing took appointment of personnel as his own responsibility; those he appointed were all men of the moment's choice. He rewarded integrity and retirement and restrained scrambling for office.
translations.idiomatic: Junqing made appointments his personal charge, choosing the best men of the day, rewarding integrity and restraining the scramble for office.

sentences.zh: 或才可用，資歷淺，密薦於上，未嘗語人。

translations.literal: If someone's talent could be used though his seniority was shallow, he would secretly recommend him to the emperor and never tell others.
translations.idiomatic: If a man of talent lacked seniority, he recommended him secretly to the emperor and never told others.

sentences.zh: 每接朝士及牧守自遠至，必問以時政得失，人才賢否。

translations.literal: Whenever he received court officials or regional governors who came from afar, he always asked about the gains and losses of current policy and whether men of talent were worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he met court officials or regional governors from afar, he always asked about current policy and the worth of available talent.

sentences.zh: 虞允文宣撫四川，俊卿薦其才堪相。

translations.literal: Yu Yunwen was pacification commissioner of Sichuan; Junqing recommended that his talent qualified him for the chief ministership.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen was pacification commissioner of Sichuan; Junqing recommended him as qualified for the chief ministership.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，上召允文為樞密使，至則以為右相，俊卿為左相。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year the emperor summoned Yunwen as commissioner of military affairs; when he arrived he was made right chief councilor and Junqing left chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year the emperor summoned Yunwen as commissioner of military affairs; on his arrival Yunwen became right chief councilor and Junqing left chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 允文建議遣使金以陵寢為請，俊卿面陳，復手疏以為未可。

translations.literal: Yunwen proposed sending envoys to the Jin to request the imperial tombs. Junqing stated his views in person and again wrote by hand that it was not yet feasible.
translations.idiomatic: Yunwen proposed sending envoys to the Jin to demand the return of the imperial tombs. Junqing argued against it in person and again wrote privately that the time was not right.

sentences.zh: 上御孤矢，弦激致目眚，六月始御便殿。

translations.literal: The emperor drew the solitary bow; the string snapped and injured his eye. Only in the sixth month did he resume holding court in the side hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor drew his bow; the string snapped and injured his eye. He did not hold court in the side hall until the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 俊卿疏曰：「陛下經月不御外朝，口語籍籍，皆輔相無狀，不能先事開陳，虧損聖德。

translations.literal: Junqing memorialized: "Your Majesty for a month has not held outer court; rumors abound, all blaming the chief ministers for misconduct in failing to speak beforehand and thereby impairing Your Majesty's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Junqing memorialized: "Your Majesty has not held outer court for a month, and rumor blames the chief ministers for failing to speak beforehand and thus impairing your virtue.

sentences.zh: 陛下憂勤恭儉，清靜寡欲，前代英主所不能免者皆屏絕，顧於騎射之末猶未能忘。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is diligent, respectful, and frugal, pure and with few desires—you have put aside what even enlightened rulers of former ages could not avoid, yet in the minor matter of riding and archery you have not yet been able to forget.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is diligent, frugal, and pure, having put aside what even former enlightened rulers could not avoid—yet you have not yet given up riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 臣知非樂此，志圖恢復，故俯而從事，以閱武備，激士氣耳。

translations.literal: Your servant knows you do not delight in this but aim at restoration, and therefore stooped to engage in it to review military readiness and rouse the troops' spirit.
translations.idiomatic: I know you do not delight in this but pursue restoration, and therefore stooped to it to review military readiness and rouse the troops' spirit.

sentences.zh: 願陛下任智謀，明賞罰，恢信義，則英聲義烈，不越尊俎，固已震懾敵人於萬里之遠，豈待區區騎射于百步間哉。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to employ wisdom and strategy, clarify rewards and punishments, and restore faith and righteousness—then heroic reputation and righteous valor, without leaving the council table, will already awe the enemy ten thousand li away. Why wait for petty riding and archery within a hundred paces?
translations.idiomatic: Employ wisdom and strategy, clarify rewards and punishments, and restore faith and righteousness—then your heroic reputation alone, without leaving the council table, will awe the enemy ten thousand li away. Why rely on petty archery at a hundred paces?

sentences.zh: 陛下一身，宗社生靈之休戚繫焉，願以今日之事，永為後戒。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty's person alone binds the fortune of the altars of state and the lives of the people; I beg that today's affair be an eternal warning hereafter."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's person alone binds the fate of the dynasty and the people; may today's affair be an eternal warning."

sentences.zh: 曾覿官滿當代，俊卿預請處以浙東總管。

translations.literal: When Zeng Di's term expired and he was due for replacement, Junqing beforehand requested that he be placed as commander-general of eastern Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Di's term expired, Junqing requested in advance that he be posted as commander-general of eastern Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「覿意似不欲為此官。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Di seems unwilling to take this post."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Di seems unwilling to take that post."

sentences.zh: 俊卿曰：「前此陛下去二人，公論甚愜。

translations.literal: Junqing said: "Previously Your Majesty removed two men, and public opinion was greatly satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Junqing said, "When Your Majesty removed those two men, public opinion was greatly satisfied.

sentences.zh: 願捐私恩，伸公議。」

translations.literal: I beg you to set aside private favor and uphold public opinion."
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to set aside private favor and uphold public opinion."

sentences.zh: 覿怏怏而去。

translations.literal: Di departed resentfully.
translations.idiomatic: Di departed in resentment.

sentences.zh: 樞密承旨張說為親戚求官，憚俊卿不敢言，會在告，請于允文，得之。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue, secretariat drafter of the Bureau of Military Affairs, sought an office for a relative but feared Junqing and did not speak. When Junqing was on leave he asked Yunwen and obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue, secretariat drafter of the Bureau of Military Affairs, sought an office for a relative but feared Junqing and said nothing. While Junqing was on leave he asked Yunwen and obtained the appointment.

sentences.zh: 俊卿聞敕已出，語吏留之。

translations.literal: Junqing heard the edict had already been issued and told the clerks to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Junqing heard the edict had been issued and ordered the clerks to hold it.

sentences.zh: 說惶恐來謝，允文亦愧，猶為之請，俊卿竟不與，說深憾之。

translations.literal: Yue came in alarm to apologize; Yunwen was also ashamed but still pleaded for him. Junqing in the end would not grant it, and Yue deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue came in alarm to apologize; Yunwen was ashamed but still pleaded for him. Junqing refused, and Yue deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書汪應辰與允文議事不合，求去，俊卿數奏應辰剛毅正直，可為執政。

translations.literal: Wang Yingchen, minister of personnel, disagreed with Yunwen on policy and sought to leave. Junqing repeatedly memorialized that Yingchen was firm, upright, and fit for the chief council.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yingchen, minister of personnel, clashed with Yunwen on policy and sought to resign. Junqing repeatedly urged that Yingchen was firm, upright, and fit for the chief council.

sentences.zh: 上初然之，後竟出應辰守平江。

translations.literal: The emperor at first agreed, but in the end sent Yingchen out to guard Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at first agreed, but in the end sent Yingchen to guard Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 自是上意向允文，而俊卿亦數求去。

translations.literal: From this time the emperor's inclination favored Yunwen, and Junqing also repeatedly sought to leave.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the emperor favored Yunwen, and Junqing repeatedly sought to resign.

sentences.zh: 明年，允文復申陵寢之議，上手劄諭俊卿，俊卿奏：「陛下痛念祖宗，思復故疆，臣雖疲駑，豈不知激昂仰贊聖謨，然于大事欲計其萬全，俟一二年間，吾之事力稍充乃可，不敢迎合意指誤國事。」

translations.literal: The next year Yunwen again raised the tomb issue. The emperor sent a hand note instructing Junqing. Junqing memorialized: "Your Majesty grieves for the ancestors and thinks of recovering the old territory. Though your servant is worn and slow, how could I not know to be stirred and support the sage plan? Yet in great affairs one must plan for complete safety. Wait one or two years until our strength is somewhat fuller—only then is it possible. I dare not flatter Your Majesty's intent and err in state affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The next year Yunwen again raised the tomb issue. The emperor sent a personal note to Junqing, who replied: "Your Majesty grieves for the ancestors and yearns to recover lost territory. Though I am worn and slow, how could I fail to support your plan? Yet great affairs require complete safety. Wait one or two years until our strength is fuller—I dare not flatter your intent and err in state affairs."

sentences.zh: 即杜門請去，以觀文殿大學士帥福州。

translations.literal: He thereupon shut his doors and asked to leave, and was made academician of the Guanwen Hall and commander of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He shut his doors and resigned, and was made academician of the Guanwen Hall and posted to command Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，猶勸上遠佞親賢，修政攘敵，泛使未可輕遣。

translations.literal: At his farewell audience he still urged the emperor to keep the wicked at a distance and be close to the worthy, reform government and repel the enemy, and not lightly send general envoys.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience he still urged the emperor to keep the wicked at a distance, cherish the worthy, reform government, repel the enemy, and not lightly send general envoys.

sentences.zh: 既去，允文卒遣使，終不得要領。

translations.literal: After he left, Yunwen in the end sent envoys but never obtained the essential point.
translations.idiomatic: After he left, Yunwen sent envoys anyway but achieved nothing of substance.

sentences.zh: 曾覿亦召還，建節鉞，躋保傅，而士大夫莫敢言。

translations.literal: Zeng Di was also recalled, granted a military commission, and advanced to guardian and tutor ranks, while scholar-officials dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Di was also recalled, granted a military commission, and advanced to guardian and tutor ranks, while officials dared not speak out.

sentences.zh: 俊卿至福州，政尚寬厚，嚴於治盜，海道晏清，以功進秩。

translations.literal: When Junqing reached Fuzhou, his government favored leniency and breadth but was strict in punishing bandits. The sea routes were peaceful, and he was promoted in rank for merit.
translations.idiomatic: At Fuzhou Junqing governed with leniency but punished bandits strictly; the sea routes grew peaceful, and he was promoted for merit.

sentences.zh: 轉運判官陳峴建議改行鈔鹽法，俊卿移書宰執，極言福建鹽法與淮、浙異，遂不果行。

translations.literal: Chen Xian, transport judicial commissioner, proposed changing to the paper-salt law. Junqing wrote the chief ministers, stating at length that Fujian's salt law differed from Huai and Zhe, and the plan was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xian, transport judicial commissioner, proposed adopting the paper-salt law. Junqing wrote the chief ministers arguing that Fujian's salt system differed from the Huai and Zhe regions, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 明年，請祠，提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: The next year he requested a sinecure and was made superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he requested leave and was made superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 歸第，弊屋數楹，怡然不介意。

translations.literal: Returning to his residence, he had only a few dilapidated rooms and was content without concern.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to a residence of only a few dilapidated rooms and was content.

sentences.zh: 淳熙二年，再命知福州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunxi he was again ordered to govern Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunxi he was again appointed prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 累章告歸，除特進，起判建康府兼江東安撫。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized to return home, was made specially advanced, and was summoned to serve as prefect of Jiankang and concurrently pacification commissioner of Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked to retire, was made specially advanced, and was summoned to serve as prefect of Jiankang and pacification commissioner of Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 召對垂拱殿，命坐賜茶，因從容言曰：「將帥當由公選，臣聞諸將多以賄得。

translations.literal: Summoned to audience in the Hall of Chui'gong, he was ordered to sit and given tea. He then spoke at ease: "Generals should be chosen by public selection. Your servant hears that many commanders obtain their posts mostly through bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to audience in the Hall of Chui'gong, he was seated and served tea. He said at ease, "Generals should be chosen openly. I hear many commanders buy their posts with bribes.

sentences.zh: 曾覿、王抃招權納賄，進人皆以中批行之。

translations.literal: Zeng Di and Wang Bian monopolize power and accept bribes; promotions are all carried out by inner drafts.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Di and Wang Bian monopolize power and accept bribes; promotions are all carried out by inner drafts.

sentences.zh: 贓吏已經結勘，而內批改正，將何所勸懲？」

translations.literal: Corrupt officials have already been investigated and concluded, yet inner drafts reverse the findings—how can there be encouragement and punishment?"
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt officials have already been investigated, yet inner drafts reverse the findings—how can discipline be maintained?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿言甚當。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words are very apt."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You speak rightly."

sentences.zh: 朝辭，奏曰：「去國十年，見都城穀賤人安，惟士大夫風俗大變。」

translations.literal: At his farewell audience he memorialized: "Having left the capital ten years, I see grain cheap and the people at peace in the metropolis, but the customs of scholar-officials have greatly changed."
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience he said, "After ten years away I find grain cheap and the people at peace in the capital, but the customs of officials have greatly changed."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「何也？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How so?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "How so?"

sentences.zh: 俊卿曰：「向士大夫奔覿、抃之門，十纏一二，尚畏人知，今則公然趨附已七八，不復顧忌矣。

translations.literal: Junqing said: "Formerly scholar-officials who rushed to Di's and Bian's doors were one or two in ten and still feared being known; now seven or eight openly rush to attach themselves without further scruple.
translations.idiomatic: Junqing said, "Formerly only one or two in ten officials courted Di and Bian, and still feared being known; now seven or eight openly attach themselves without scruple.

sentences.zh: 人材進退由私門，大非朝廷美事。」

translations.literal: The advancement and dismissal of talent through private doors is greatly not a fine affair for the court."
translations.idiomatic: When appointments pass through private doors, that is no fine thing for the court."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「抃則不敢。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "As for Bian, I would not dare.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "As for Bian, I would not dare.

sentences.zh: 覿雖時或有請，朕多抑之，自今不復從矣。」

translations.literal: Though Di sometimes makes requests, I mostly restrain them; from now on I will no longer comply."
translations.idiomatic: Though Di sometimes makes requests, I mostly refuse them; from now on I will no longer comply."

sentences.zh: 俊卿曰：「此曹聲勢既長，侍從、臺諫多出其門，毋敢為陛下言，臣恐壞朝廷紀綱，廢有司法度，敗天下風俗，累陛下聖德。」

translations.literal: Junqing said: "These men's power has already grown long; many attendants and censors come from their doors and dare not speak for Your Majesty. Your servant fears they will ruin court discipline, abolish established law, corrupt the world's customs, and burden Your Majesty's sacred virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Junqing said, "These men's influence has grown; many attendants and censors come from their faction and dare not speak for Your Majesty. I fear they will ruin court discipline, abolish the law, corrupt public morals, and burden your sacred virtue."

sentences.zh: 命二府飲餞浙江亭。

translations.literal: He ordered the two chief councils to give a farewell feast at Zhejiang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The two chief councils were ordered to give him a farewell feast at Zhejiang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 俊卿去建康十五年，父老喜其再來。

translations.literal: Fifteen years after Junqing left Jiankang, the elders rejoiced at his return.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen years after Junqing had left Jiankang, the elders rejoiced at his return.

sentences.zh: 為政寬簡，罷無名之賦。

translations.literal: His government was lenient and simple; he abolished irregular levies.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with leniency and simplicity and abolished irregular levies.

sentences.zh: 時御前多行「白劄」，用左右私人持送，俊卿奏非便，上手劄獎諭。

translations.literal: At that time many "white memorials" were issued from the imperial presence, carried by private attendants on the left and right. Junqing memorialized that this was not expedient, and the emperor sent a hand note commending and instructing him.
translations.idiomatic: Many "white memorials" were then issued from the imperial presence and carried by private attendants. Junqing objected that this was unwise, and the emperor sent a personal note commending him.

sentences.zh: 除少保，判建康府如故。

translations.literal: He was made junior guardian and continued as prefect of Jiankang as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made junior guardian and continued as prefect of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 八年上章告老，以少師、魏國公致仕。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he memorialized to retire on account of age and was made junior preceptor and Duke of Wei, retiring from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he petitioned to retire and was made junior preceptor and Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 十三年十一月薨，年七十四。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the thirteenth year he died, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the thirteenth year he died, aged seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 方屬疾，手書示諸子云：「遺表止謝聖恩，勿祈恩澤及功德，勿請諡樹碑。」

translations.literal: While ill he wrote by hand to show his sons: "The final memorial should only thank the sage grace; do not seek favors and merit, and do not request a posthumous title or stele."
translations.idiomatic: While ill he wrote to his sons: "My final memorial should only thank the emperor; do not seek favors, merit titles, posthumous names, or steles."

sentences.zh: 上聞嗟悼，輟視朝，贈太保，命本路轉運司給葬事，賜諡「正獻」。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he sighed in grief, suspended court audiences, posthumously made him grand guardian, ordered the circuit transport office to provide funeral arrangements, and granted the posthumous title "Righteous Presentation."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved, suspended court, posthumously made him grand guardian, ordered the transport office to arrange the funeral, and granted the posthumous title "Righteous Presentation."

sentences.zh: 俊卿孝友忠敬，得於天資，清嚴好禮，終日無惰容。

translations.literal: Junqing was filial, friendly, loyal, and respectful by inborn nature; pure, stern, and fond of ritual, all day without a lazy countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Junqing was filial, loyal, and respectful by nature; grave, austere, and fond of ritual, never showing a lazy bearing all day.

sentences.zh: 平居恂恂若不能言，而在朝廷正色危論，分別邪正，斥權勢無顧避。

translations.literal: In ordinary life he was modest as if unable to speak, yet in court he spoke with stern countenance and weighty argument, distinguishing the wicked from the upright and denouncing power without regard for avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: In private he was modest as if unable to speak, yet in court he spoke with grave bearing, distinguished right from wrong, and denounced the powerful without fear.

sentences.zh: 凡所奏請，關治亂安危之大者。

translations.literal: All his memorials and requests concerned great matters of order and chaos, safety and peril.
translations.idiomatic: All his memorials concerned great matters of order and chaos, safety and peril.

sentences.zh: 雅善汪應辰、李燾，尤敬朱熹，屢嘗論薦。

translations.literal: He was on excellent terms with Wang Yingchen and Li Tao, and especially respected Zhu Xi, repeatedly discussing and recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Wang Yingchen and Li Tao and especially respected Zhu Xi, whom he repeatedly recommended.

sentences.zh: 其薨也，熹不遠千里往哭之，又狀其行。

translations.literal: At his death Xi traveled a thousand li to mourn him and also composed an account of his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: At his death Zhu Xi traveled a thousand li to mourn him and composed an account of his conduct.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 子五人，宓有志於學，終承奉郎，朱熹為銘其墓。

translations.literal: He had five sons. Mi aspired to learning and ended as gentleman for court attendance; Zhu Xi composed the inscription for his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons. Mi aspired to learning and ended as gentleman for court attendance; Zhu Xi wrote the inscription for his tomb.

sentences.zh: 宓自有傳。

translations.literal: Mi has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Mi has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 虞允文

translations.literal: Yu Yunwen
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen

sentences.zh: 虞允文，字彬甫，隆州仁壽人。

translations.literal: Yu Yunwen, styled Binfu, was a man of Renshou in Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen, whose courtesy name was Binfu, came from Renshou in Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 父祺，登政和進士第，仕至太常博士、潼川路轉運判官。

translations.literal: His father Qi passed the jinshi in the Zhenghe era and served up to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and judicial commissioner of transport on the Tongchuan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qi passed the jinshi in the Zhenghe era and rose to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and transport judicial commissioner on the Tongchuan circuit.

sentences.zh: 允文六歲誦《九經》，七歲能屬文。

translations.literal: At six Yunwen could recite the Nine Classics; at seven he could compose prose.
translations.idiomatic: At six he could recite the Nine Classics; at seven he could compose prose.

sentences.zh: 以父任入官。

translations.literal: He entered office through his father's privilege.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office through his father's privilege.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，哀毀骨立。

translations.literal: When his mother died he mourned so grievously that only skin and bone remained.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he mourned so grievously that he was reduced to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 既葬，朝夕哭墓側，墓有枯桑，兩烏來巢。

translations.literal: After burial he wept morning and evening beside the tomb. At the tomb was a withered mulberry, and two crows came to nest.
translations.idiomatic: After burial he wept morning and evening at the tomb, where a withered mulberry stood and two crows came to nest.

sentences.zh: 念父之鰥且疾，七年不調，跬步不忍離左右。

translations.literal: Thinking that his father was widowed and ill, for seven years he did not take a new post and could not bear to leave his father's side even a step.
translations.idiomatic: His father was widowed and ill; for seven years he took no new post and would not leave his father's side even a step.

sentences.zh: 父死，紹興二十三年始登進士第，通判彭州，權知黎州、渠州。

translations.literal: When his father died, in the twenty-third year of Shaoxing he first passed the jinshi, became vice-prefect of Pengzhou, and acted as prefect of Lizhou and Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he passed the jinshi in the twenty-third year of Shaoxing, became vice-prefect of Pengzhou, and acted as prefect of Lizhou and Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 秦檜當國，蜀士多屏棄。

translations.literal: When Qin Hui held power, many scholars of Shu were cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Hui held power, many scholars of Shu were cast aside.

sentences.zh: 檜死，高宗欲收用之，中書舍人趙達首薦允文，召對，謂人君必畏天，必安民，必法祖宗。

translations.literal: When Hui died, Gaozong wished to bring him back into service. Drafting officer Zhao Da was the first to recommend Yunwen. Summoned for audience, he said a ruler must fear Heaven, must secure the people, and must take the ancestors as his law.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin Hui died, Emperor Gaozong wished to bring Yu Yunwen back into service. Palace drafting officer Zhao Da was the first to recommend him. Summoned for an audience, Yunwen said that a ruler must fear Heaven, secure the people, and take the ancestors as his law.

sentences.zh: 又論士風之弊，以文章進必抑其輕浮，以言語進必黜其巧偽，以政事進必去其苛刻，庶可任重致遠。

translations.literal: He also discussed the defects of scholarly conduct: those who advanced through literary skill must have their frivolity checked; those who advanced through eloquence must have their cunning falsehood dismissed; those who advanced through administrative affairs must have their harshness removed—only then could they bear heavy responsibility and reach far.
translations.idiomatic: He also discussed the defects of scholarly culture: those promoted for literary talent must be checked for frivolity; those promoted for eloquence must be dismissed for cunning deceit; those promoted for administrative skill must be purged of harshness—only then could they bear heavy responsibility and achieve lasting results.

sentences.zh: 且極論四川財賦科納之弊。

translations.literal: Moreover he spoke exhaustively on the abuses of Sichuan's fiscal levies and collections.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke at length about the abuses of Sichuan's fiscal levies and tax collections.

sentences.zh: 上嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his advice and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 除秘書丞，累遷禮部郎官。

translations.literal: He was appointed secretary of the Secretariat and, through successive promotions, became an official of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed secretary of the Secretariat and was successively promoted to posts in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 金主亮修汴，已有南侵意。

translations.literal: The Jin ruler Hailing repaired Bianjing and already had the intention of invading south.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor Hailing had Bianjing repaired and already intended to invade the south.

sentences.zh: 王倫還，言敵恭順和好。

translations.literal: Wang Lun returned and reported that the enemy was deferential and sought good relations.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lun returned from the Jin court, he reported that the enemy was deferential and eager for peace.

sentences.zh: 湯思退再拜賀，置邊備不問。

translations.literal: Tang Situi twice bowed in congratulation and put border defense out of mind.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Situi bowed in congratulation and gave no thought to border defenses.

sentences.zh: 及金使施宜生頗泄敵情，張燾密奏之。

translations.literal: When the Jin envoy Shi Yisheng rather leaked enemy intelligence, Zhang Tao secretly memorialized this.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin envoy Shi Yisheng let slip considerable intelligence about the enemy, Zhang Tao secretly reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 亮又隱畫工圖臨安湖山以歸。

translations.literal: Hailing also secretly sent painters to make pictures of Lin'an's lakes and mountains and took them back.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing also secretly sent painters to depict the lakes and mountains of Lin'an and took the paintings back with him.

sentences.zh: 亮賦詩，情益露。

translations.literal: Hailing composed poems, and his intentions became still more evident.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing composed poems, his hostile intentions became still more obvious.

sentences.zh: 允文上疏言：「金必敗盟，兵出有五道，願詔大臣豫思備禦。」

translations.literal: Yunwen submitted a memorial saying: "The Jin will surely break the treaty. Their troops will come by five routes. I pray that ministers be instructed beforehand to think of defense."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen submitted a memorial stating, "The Jin will surely break the treaty. Their army will advance along five routes. I ask that ministers be ordered in advance to prepare defenses."

sentences.zh: 時三十年正月也。

translations.literal: This was in the first month of the thirtieth year.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the first month of the thirtieth year of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 十月，借工部尚書充賀正使，與館伴賓射，一發破的，眾驚異之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, on temporary appointment as minister of works he served as envoy offering New Year's congratulations. At banquet archery with the reception staff, with one shot he hit the target, and the crowd was startled and amazed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he temporarily served as minister of works and envoy offering New Year's congratulations. At an archery contest with the reception staff, he hit the target with his first shot, to everyone's astonishment.

sentences.zh: 允文見運糧造舟者多，辭歸，亮曰：「我將看花洛陽。」

translations.literal: Yunwen saw many men transporting grain and building boats. When he took leave to return, Hailing said: "I will go view the flowers at Luoyang."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen noticed many men transporting grain and building boats. As he took leave to return home, Hailing said, "I plan to go view the flowers at Luoyang."

sentences.zh: 允文還，奏所見及亮語，申言淮、海之備。

translations.literal: When Yunwen returned, he memorialized what he had seen and Hailing's words, reiterating the need to prepare the Huai and sea fronts.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Yunwen returned, he reported what he had seen and Hailing's remark, urging preparations along the Huai River and the coast.

sentences.zh: 除中書舍人、直學士院。

translations.literal: He was appointed drafting officer of the Secretariat and academician of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed drafting officer of the Secretariat and academician of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 三衙管軍以宦寺充承受，允文言：「自古人主大權，不移于姦臣，則落於近幸。

translations.literal: The Three Commands entrusted military administration to eunuchs serving as liaisons. Yunwen said: "Since antiquity a ruler's great power, if not transferred to treacherous ministers, then fell into the hands of those close at hand.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Commands had eunuchs serve as military liaisons. Yu Yunwen said, "Throughout history, when a ruler's supreme authority did not pass to treacherous ministers, it fell into the hands of favorites at court.

sentences.zh: 秦檜盜權十有八年，檜死，權歸陛下。

translations.literal: Qin Hui usurped power for fully eighteen years. When Hui died, power returned to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui seized power for fully eighteen years. When he died, authority returned to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 邇來三衙交結中官，宣和、明受厥鑒未遠。」

translations.literal: Recently the Three Commands have formed ties with palace eunuchs—the lessons of Xuanhe and the Ming Shou incident are not far off."
translations.idiomatic: Recently the Three Commands have cultivated ties with palace eunuchs—the lessons of the Xuanhe era and the Ming Shou affair are not far in the past."

sentences.zh: 上大悟，立罷之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enlightened and immediately abolished the practice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly enlightened and immediately abolished the practice.

sentences.zh: 金使王全、高景山來賀生辰，口傳亮悖慢語，欲得淮南地，索將相大臣議事。

translations.literal: Jin envoys Wang Quan and Gao Jingshan came to congratulate the emperor's birthday. They orally transmitted Hailing's insolent words, demanding the land south of the Huai, and requested that chief and assistant ministers come to negotiate.
translations.idiomatic: Jin envoys Wang Quan and Gao Jingshan came to congratulate the emperor on his birthday. They relayed Hailing's insolent message, demanding territory south of the Huai River and insisting that chief and assistant ministers come to negotiate.

sentences.zh: 於是召三衙大將趙密等議舉兵，侍從、臺諫集議。

translations.literal: Thereupon the great generals of the Three Commands, Zhao Mi and others, were summoned to discuss raising troops, and attendant and remonstrance officials gathered for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The court then summoned the senior generals of the Three Commands, including Zhao Mi, to discuss mobilizing for war, and assembled attendant and remonstrance officials for joint deliberation.

sentences.zh: 宰臣陳康伯傳上旨：「今日更不問和與守，直問戰當如何。」

translations.literal: Chief minister Chen Kangbo conveyed the emperor's intent: "Today we no longer ask about peace or defense—we ask directly how war should be conducted."
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Chen Kangbo conveyed the emperor's command: "Today we will no longer debate peace or passive defense—we will ask directly how to fight."

sentences.zh: 遣成閔為京湖制置使，將禁衛五萬禦襄、漢上流。

translations.literal: Cheng Min was dispatched as commissioner for the Jing-Hu region, leading fifty thousand imperial guards to defend the upper Xiang and Han rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Min was dispatched as Jing-Hu commissioner, leading fifty thousand imperial guards to defend the upper reaches of the Xiang and Han rivers.

sentences.zh: 允文曰：「兵來不除道，敵為虛聲以分我兵，成其出淮姦謀爾。」

translations.literal: Yunwen said: "When troops come they do not clear the roads—this is the enemy's feint to divide our forces and accomplish their plot to strike from the Huai."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen said, "When enemy troops advance they do not clear roads ahead of them—the enemy is feinting to divide our forces and cover their real scheme to break out from the Huai."

sentences.zh: 不聽，卒遣閔。

translations.literal: His advice was not heeded, and in the end Min was dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not listen, and Cheng Min was dispatched anyway.

sentences.zh: 七月，金主亮徙汴，允文復語康伯：「閔軍約程在江、池，宜令到池者駐池，到江者駐江。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, the Jin ruler Hailing moved to Bianjing. Yunwen again told Kangbo: "Min's army by schedule should reach Jiang and Chi—those who reach Chi should encamp at Chi, those who reach Jiang should encamp at Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Jin emperor Hailing moved his court to Bianjing. Yu Yunwen again told Chen Kangbo, "By schedule Cheng Min's army should reach Chizhou and Jiangzhou. Those who reach Chizhou should encamp there; those who reach Jiangzhou should encamp there.

sentences.zh: 若敵兵出上流，則荊湖之軍捍于前，江、池之軍援於後；

translations.literal: If enemy troops come from the upper stream, then the Jing-Hu armies would hold them in front and the Jiang and Chi armies support from behind;
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy came from the upper river, the Jing-Hu armies could hold them in front while the Chizhou and Jiangzhou forces reinforced from behind;

sentences.zh: 若出淮西，則池之軍出巢縣，江州軍出無為，可為淮西援，是一軍而兩用之。」

translations.literal: if they came from west of the Huai, then Chi's army would sortie from Chaoxian and Jiangzhou's army from Wuwei, and could serve as reinforcements for the Huai west—a single army used in two ways."
translations.idiomatic: if they came from west of the Huai, the Chizhou army could sortie from Chaoxian and the Jiangzhou army from Wuwei to reinforce the Huai west—one army deployed in two directions."

sentences.zh: 康伯然其說，而閔軍竟屯武昌。

translations.literal: Kangbo agreed with this plan, but Min's army in the end encamped at Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Kangbo agreed with the plan, but Cheng Min's army ultimately encamped at Wuchang instead.

sentences.zh: 九月，金主命李通為大都督，造浮梁于淮水上。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the Jin ruler appointed Li Tong supreme commander and built floating bridges on the Huai River.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Jin emperor appointed Li Tong supreme commander and built floating bridges on the Huai River.

sentences.zh: 金主自將，兵號百萬，氈帳相望，鉦鼓之聲不絕。

translations.literal: The Jin ruler commanded in person. His army was said to number a million; felt tents stretched from sight to sight, and the sound of gongs and drums never ceased.
