translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor took personal command. His army was said to number a million; felt tents stretched as far as the eye could see, and the clamor of gongs and drums never ceased.

sentences.zh: 十月，自渦口渡淮。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he crossed the Huai from Wokou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he crossed the Huai at Wokou.

sentences.zh: 先是，劉錡措置淮東，王權措置淮西。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu Qi had managed Huai east and Wang Quan Huai west.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Qi had been managing the Huai east region and Wang Quan the Huai west region.

sentences.zh: 至是，權首棄廬州，錡亦回揚州，中外震恐。

translations.literal: At this point Quan was the first to abandon Luzhou, and Qi also withdrew to Yangzhou. Court and country were shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Wang Quan was the first to abandon Luzhou, and Liu Qi also withdrew to Yangzhou. The court and the country were shaken with terror.

sentences.zh: 上欲航海，陳康伯力贊親征。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to flee by sea; Chen Kangbo strongly urged him to take the field in person.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to flee by sea, but Chen Kangbo strongly urged him to lead the campaign in person.

sentences.zh: 是月戊午，樞臣葉義問督江、淮軍，允文參謀軍事。

translations.literal: On wuwu day of that month, chief councillor Ye Yiwen supervised the Jiang and Huai armies, and Yunwen served as military adviser.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day of that month, chief councillor Ye Yiwen took command of the Jiang and Huai armies, with Yu Yunwen as military adviser.

sentences.zh: 權又自和州遁歸，錡回鎮江，盡失兩淮矣。

translations.literal: Quan again fled from Hezhou. Qi returned to Zhenjiang. Both banks of the Huai were entirely lost.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Quan fled again from Hezhou, and Liu Qi withdrew to Zhenjiang—the entire Huai region was lost.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬申，金主率大軍臨采石，而別以兵爭瓜洲。

translations.literal: On renshen day of the eleventh month, the Jin ruler led a great army to Caishi while another force contended for Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen day of the eleventh month, the Jin emperor led a great army to Caishi while a separate force fought for Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 朝命成閔代錡、李顯忠代權，錡、權皆召。

translations.literal: The court ordered Cheng Min to replace Qi and Li Xianzhong to replace Quan; both Qi and Quan were summoned.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Cheng Min to replace Liu Qi and Li Xianzhong to replace Wang Quan; both Liu and Wang were summoned back.

sentences.zh: 義問被旨，命允文往蕪湖趣顯忠交權軍，且犒師采石，時權軍猶在采石。

translations.literal: Ye Yiwen received orders to send Yunwen to Wuhu to urge Xianzhong to take over Quan's army and also to reward the troops at Caishi; at that time Quan's army was still at Caishi.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Yiwen received orders to send Yu Yunwen to Wuhu to hurry Li Xianzhong in relieving Wang Quan's command and also to reward the troops at Caishi, where Wang Quan's army still remained.

sentences.zh: 丙子，允文至采石，權已去，顯忠未來，敵騎充斥。

translations.literal: On bingzi day Yunwen reached Caishi. Quan had already gone, Xianzhong had not yet arrived, and enemy horsemen filled the area.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingzi day Yu Yunwen reached Caishi. Wang Quan had already fled, Li Xianzhong had not yet arrived, and enemy cavalry filled the area.

sentences.zh: 我師三五星散，解鞍束甲坐道旁，皆權敗兵也。

translations.literal: Our troops were scattered in threes and fives, had unsaddled and donned armor, and sat by the roadside—all were Quan's defeated soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Song troops were scattered in small groups of three to five, sitting unsaddled along the roadside in armor—all were remnants of Wang Quan's defeated army.

sentences.zh: 允文謂坐待顯忠則誤國事，遂立招諸將，勉以忠義，曰：「金帛、告命皆在此，待有功。」

translations.literal: Yunwen said that to sit waiting for Xianzhong would ruin the state's affairs. He immediately stood and summoned the generals, urging them with loyalty and righteousness, and said: "Gold, silk, and commission patents are all here—they await merit."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen decided that waiting passively for Li Xianzhong would betray the country. He immediately rallied the generals, exhorting them with talk of loyalty and duty, and said, "Gold, silk, and commissions are all here, waiting to reward those who distinguish themselves."

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「今既有主，請死戰。」

translations.literal: The crowd said: "Now that we have a leader, we ask to fight to the death."
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "Now that we have a leader, we ask to fight to the death."

sentences.zh: 或曰：「公受命犒師，不受命督戰，他人壞之，公任其咎乎？」

translations.literal: Someone said: "You were ordered to reward the troops, not to command battle. If others spoil things, will you bear the blame?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone objected, "You were ordered to reward the troops, not to command the battle. If others fail, will you alone bear the blame?"

sentences.zh: 允文叱之曰：「危及社稷，吾將安避？」

translations.literal: Yunwen rebuked him, saying: "When the altars of state are endangered, where shall I hide?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen rebuked him: "When the altars of state are in peril, where can I hide?"

sentences.zh: 至江濱，見江北已築高臺，對植絳旗二、繡旗二，中建黃屋，亮踞坐其下。

translations.literal: When he reached the riverbank, he saw that on the north bank a high platform had been built. Two crimson flags and two embroidered flags were planted facing each other, and in the center stood a yellow canopy. Hailing sat astride beneath it.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the riverbank, he saw that on the north bank a high platform had been erected with two crimson flags and two embroidered flags planted opposite each other and a yellow imperial canopy in the center. Hailing sat enthroned beneath it.

sentences.zh: 諜者言，前一日刑白黑馬祭天，與眾盟，以明日濟江，晨炊玉麟堂，先濟者予黃金一兩。

translations.literal: Spies reported that the day before he had sacrificed a white and a black horse to Heaven, sworn an oath with the host to cross the river the next day, breakfasted at the Hall of the Jade Unicorn, and promised one tael of gold to whoever crossed first.
translations.idiomatic: Spies reported that the day before Hailing had sacrificed white and black horses to Heaven, sworn an oath with his troops to cross the river the next day, taken breakfast at the Hall of the Jade Unicorn, and promised one tael of gold to whoever crossed first.

sentences.zh: 時敵兵實四十萬，馬倍之，宋軍才一萬八千。

translations.literal: At that time the enemy actually numbered four hundred thousand, with twice as many horses, while the Song army had only eighteen thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy in fact numbered four hundred thousand men with twice as many horses, while the Song forces totaled only eighteen thousand.

sentences.zh: 允文乃命諸將列大陣不動，分戈船為五，其二並東西岸而行，其一駐中流，藏精兵待戰，其二藏小港，備不測。

translations.literal: Yunwen then ordered the generals to form a great battle line and hold firm. He divided the war boats into five groups: two sailed along the eastern and western banks; one halted midstream with crack troops hidden for battle; two hid in small inlets against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen ordered the generals to form a battle line and hold position. He divided the oared warships into five groups: two sailed along the eastern and western banks, one held midstream with elite troops concealed for battle, and two waited hidden in small inlets against surprise.

sentences.zh: 部分甫畢，敵已大呼，亮操小紅旗麾數百艘絕江而來，瞬息，抵南岸者七十艘，直薄宋軍，軍小卻。

translations.literal: The disposition had just been completed when the enemy raised a great shout. Hailing waved a small red flag and hundreds of boats crossed the river. In an instant seventy reached the south bank, pressed straight against the Song army, and the army fell back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had the disposition been completed when the enemy raised a great shout. Hailing waved a small red flag and hundreds of boats crossed the river. In an instant seventy reached the south bank and pressed straight against the Song lines, which fell back slightly.

sentences.zh: 允文入陣中，撫時俊之背曰：「汝膽略聞四方，立陣後則兒女子爾。」

translations.literal: Yunwen entered the battle line, patted Shi Jun on the back, and said: "Your courage and strategy are known everywhere—standing behind the line makes you no better than a woman or child."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen entered the battle line, clapped Shi Jun on the back, and said, "Your courage and skill are famed throughout the land—standing behind the line makes you no better than a woman or child."

sentences.zh: 俊即揮雙刀出，士殊死戰。

translations.literal: Jun immediately swung twin swords and charged forth; the soldiers fought with extraordinary desperation.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jun immediately charged out wielding twin swords, and the soldiers fought with desperate valor.

sentences.zh: 中流官軍亦以海鰍船衝敵，舟皆平沉，敵半死半戰，日暮未退。

translations.literal: The midstream official army also used haizhao boats to ram the enemy. The boats were all sunk level; half the enemy were dead and half still fighting, and at dusk they had not withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: The midstream Song forces also rammed the enemy with paddle-wheel boats, sinking their vessels flush with the water. Half the enemy were dead and half still fighting, and by dusk they had not withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 會有潰軍自光州至，允文授以旗鼓，從山後轉出，敵疑援兵至，始遁。

translations.literal: Just then routed troops arrived from Guangzhou. Yunwen gave them banners and drums and had them emerge from behind the hills. The enemy suspected reinforcements had arrived and only then fled.
translations.idiomatic: Just then routed troops arrived from Guangzhou. Yu Yunwen gave them banners and drums and sent them around from behind the hills. The enemy, suspecting reinforcements had arrived, finally fled.

sentences.zh: 又命勁弓尾擊追射，大敗之，僵屍凡四千餘，殺萬戶二人，俘千戶五人及生女真五百餘人。

translations.literal: He also ordered strong bowmen to pursue from the rear and shoot; they inflicted a great defeat. Stiff corpses totaled more than four thousand; two wanhu were killed, five qianhu captured, and more than five hundred live Jurchens taken.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered strong bowmen to pursue and shoot from the rear, inflicting a major defeat. More than four thousand corpses littered the field; two wanhu officers were killed, five qianhu officers captured, and more than five hundred Jurchen soldiers taken alive.

sentences.zh: 敵兵不死于江者，亮悉敲殺之，怒其不出江也。

translations.literal: Enemy soldiers who had not died on the river—Hailing had them all clubbed to death, enraged that they had not crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing had all enemy soldiers who had not died on the river clubbed to death, furious that they had failed to cross.

sentences.zh: 以捷聞，犒將士，謂之曰：「敵今敗，明必復來。」

translations.literal: He reported the victory, rewarded the officers and soldiers, and told them: "The enemy is defeated today; tomorrow they will surely come again."
translations.idiomatic: He reported the victory and rewarded the officers and soldiers, telling them, "The enemy is beaten today, but tomorrow they will surely return."

sentences.zh: 夜半，部分諸將，分海舟縋上流，別遣兵截楊林口。

translations.literal: At midnight he disposed the generals, sent sea boats upstream by rope, and separately dispatched troops to block Yanglin Pass.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight he repositioned the generals, sent sea boats upstream by rope haul, and separately dispatched troops to block Yanglin Pass.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，敵果至，因夾擊之，復大戰，焚其舟三百，始遁去，再以捷聞。

translations.literal: On dingchou day the enemy indeed came. Attacked from both sides, they fought another great battle; three hundred of their boats were burned, and only then did they flee. Victory was again reported.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingchou day the enemy did return. Attacked from both flanks, they fought another major battle; three hundred of their boats were burned before they finally fled. Yu Yunwen reported victory again.

sentences.zh: 既而敵遣偽詔來諭王權，似有宿約。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the enemy sent a forged edict to instruct Wang Quan, as if there were a longstanding agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the enemy sent a forged edict addressed to Wang Quan, as if some secret agreement existed between them.

sentences.zh: 允文曰：「此反間也。」

translations.literal: Yunwen said: "This is a stratagem of alienation."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen said, "This is a stratagem to sow discord."

sentences.zh: 仍復書言：「權已置典憲，新將李世輔也，願一戰以決雌雄。」

translations.literal: He nevertheless replied by letter saying: "Quan has already been punished under military law. The new general is Li Shipu. We wish one battle to decide victory and defeat."
translations.idiomatic: He nevertheless replied, "Wang Quan has already been punished under military law. The new commander is Li Shipu. We wish to settle the matter in a single battle."

sentences.zh: 亮得書大怒，遂焚龍鳳車，斬梁漢臣及造舟者二人，乃趨瓜洲。

translations.literal: When Hailing received the letter he was furious. He then burned his dragon-and-phoenix carriage, executed Liang Hanchen and two boat-builders, and hastened to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing read the reply he flew into a rage, burned his dragon-and-phoenix carriage, executed Liang Hanchen and two shipwrights, and marched on Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 漢臣，教亮濟江者也。

translations.literal: Hanchen was the one who had taught Hailing to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Hanchen was the man who had advised Hailing on crossing the river.

sentences.zh: 顯忠至自蕪湖，允文語之曰：「敵入揚州，必與瓜洲兵合，京口無備，我當往，公能分兵相助乎？」

translations.literal: When Xianzhong arrived from Wuhu, Yunwen said to him: "When the enemy enters Yangzhou they will surely unite with the Guazhou troops. Jingkou is undefended. I must go there—can you divide your forces to help?"
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xianzhong arrived from Wuhu, Yu Yunwen told him, "When the enemy enters Yangzhou they will surely join forces with the troops at Guazhou. Jingkou is undefended. I must go there—can you detach troops to help?"

sentences.zh: 顯忠分李捧軍萬六千往京口，葉義問亦命楊存中將所部來會。

translations.literal: Xianzhong detached Li Bang's army of sixteen thousand to Jingkou. Ye Yiwen also ordered Yang Cunzhong to lead his forces to join them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xianzhong detached Li Bang's army of sixteen thousand men to Jingkou, and Ye Yiwen also ordered Yang Cunzhong to bring his forces to join them.

sentences.zh: 允文還建康，即上疏言：「敵敗於采石，將徼幸於瓜洲。

translations.literal: Yunwen returned to Jiankang and immediately submitted a memorial saying: "The enemy was defeated at Caishi and will gamble on Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen returned to Jiankang and immediately submitted a memorial stating, "Having been defeated at Caishi, the enemy will try their luck at Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 今我精兵聚京口，持重待之，可一戰而勝。

translations.literal: Now our elite troops are gathered at Jingkou. If we hold firm and wait, we can win in one battle.
translations.idiomatic: Our best troops are now gathered at Jingkou. If we hold our ground and wait, we can win in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 乞少緩六飛之發。」

translations.literal: I beg that the departure of the imperial carriage be slightly delayed."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the emperor's departure be slightly delayed."

sentences.zh: 甲申，至京口。

translations.literal: On jiashen day he reached Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day he reached Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 敵屯重兵滁河，造三閘儲水，深數尺，塞瓜洲口。

translations.literal: The enemy massed heavy troops on the Chu River, built three sluice gates to store water several feet deep, and blocked the mouth of Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy massed heavy forces along the Chu River, built three sluice gates to store water several feet deep, and blocked the mouth of Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 時楊存中、成閔、邵宏淵諸軍皆聚京口，不下二十萬，惟海鰍船不滿百，戈船半之。

translations.literal: At that time the armies of Yang Cunzhong, Cheng Min, Shao Hongyuan, and others were all gathered at Jingkou—no fewer than two hundred thousand—yet haizhao boats numbered fewer than a hundred and war boats only half that.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the armies of Yang Cunzhong, Cheng Min, Shao Hongyuan, and others had all gathered at Jingkou—no fewer than two hundred thousand men—but paddle-wheel boats numbered fewer than a hundred and oared warships only half as many.

sentences.zh: 允文謂遇風則使戰船，無風則使戰艦，數少恐不足用。

translations.literal: Yunwen said that when there was wind they would use combat boats, and when there was no wind combat ships—but with so few they feared they would not suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen noted that in wind they would need lighter combat boats and in calm weather heavier warships, and feared that they had too few of either.

sentences.zh: 遂聚材治鐵，改修馬船為戰艦，且借之平江，命張深守滁河口，扼大江之衝，以苗定駐下蜀為援。

translations.literal: He therefore gathered timber and worked iron, converted transport boats into warships, and also borrowed them from Pingjiang. He ordered Zhang Shen to hold the Chu River mouth and guard the great river's key point, with Miao Ding encamped at Xiasbu as reinforcement.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore gathered timber and iron, converted transport boats into warships, and also requisitioned vessels from Pingjiang. He ordered Zhang Shen to hold the Chu River mouth and guard the Yangtze crossing, with Miao Ding encamped at Xiasbu as reinforcement.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，亮至瓜洲，允文與存中臨江按試，命戰士踏車船中流上下，三周金山，回轉如飛，敵持滿以待，相顧駭愕。

translations.literal: On gengyin day Hailing reached Guazhou. Yunwen and Cunzhong inspected along the river, ordering warriors to pedal the boat-ships up and down midstream. Three circuits around Mount Jin, turning like flight—the enemy stood with bows drawn waiting and looked at one another in shock.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day Hailing reached Guazhou. Yu Yunwen and Yang Cunzhong inspected their forces along the river, ordering warriors to pedal their boat-ships up and down midstream. They circled Mount Jin three times, wheeling about with startling speed. The enemy stood with bows drawn waiting and stared at one another in astonishment.

sentences.zh: 亮笑曰：「紙船耳。」

translations.literal: Hailing laughed and said: "Paper boats, that's all."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing laughed and said, "They're only paper boats."

sentences.zh: 一將跪奏：「南軍有備，未可輕，願駐揚州，徐圖進取。」

translations.literal: A general knelt and reported: "The southern army is prepared; we must not take them lightly. I ask that we encamp at Yangzhou and slowly plan an advance."
translations.idiomatic: A general knelt and reported, "The southern army is prepared and must not be underestimated. I ask that we halt at Yangzhou and plan our advance more carefully."

sentences.zh: 亮怒，欲斬之，哀謝良久，杖之五十。

translations.literal: Hailing was enraged and wished to behead him. After long pleading he was spared, but was beaten fifty blows with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing flew into a rage and wanted to behead him. After prolonged pleading the man was spared but flogged fifty strokes.

sentences.zh: 乙未，亮為其下所殺。

translations.literal: On yimi day Hailing was killed by his own subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimi day Hailing was assassinated by his own officers.

sentences.zh: 初，亮在瓜洲，聞李寶由海道入膠西，成閔諸軍方順流而下，亮愈怒。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Hailing was at Guazhou, he heard that Li Bao had entered Jiaoxi by sea route and that Cheng Min's armies were sailing downstream—Hailing grew still angrier.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Hailing was at Guazhou, he heard that Li Bao had invaded Jiaoxi by sea and that Cheng Min's armies were sailing downstream—Hailing grew still angrier.

sentences.zh: 還揚州，召諸將約三日濟江，否則盡殺之。

translations.literal: Returning to Yangzhou, he summoned the generals and set three days to cross the river, or else he would kill them all.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Yangzhou, he summoned his generals and gave them three days to cross the river—or he would execute them all.

sentences.zh: 諸將謀曰：「進有渰殺之禍，退有敲殺之憂，奈何？」

translations.literal: The generals plotted, saying: "To advance brings the calamity of drowning death; to retreat brings the worry of clubbing death—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The generals conferred: "Advancing means drowning in the river; retreating means being clubbed to death. What can we do?"

sentences.zh: 有萬戴者曰：「殺郎主，與南宋通和歸鄉則生矣。」

translations.literal: One Wan Dai said: "Kill the prince-lord, make peace with the Southern Song, and return home—then we shall live."
translations.idiomatic: A man named Wan Dai said, "Kill the prince-lord, make peace with the Southern Song, and return home—we can live."

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「諾。」

translations.literal: The crowd said: "Agreed."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Agreed."

sentences.zh: 亮有紫茸細軍，不臨陣，恒以自衛，眾患之，有蕭遮巴者紿之曰：「淮東子女玉帛皆聚海陵。」

translations.literal: Hailing had a purple-fur elite guard that did not enter battle but always guarded him personally; the host resented this. One Xiao Zheba deceived him, saying: "The women, children, jade, and silk of Huai east are all gathered at Hailing."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing kept an elite guard clothed in purple fur that never entered battle but always protected him personally, which the troops resented. A man named Xiao Zheba deceived him, saying, "The women, riches, and goods of Huai east are all gathered at Hailing."

sentences.zh: 且嗾使往，細軍去而亮死。

translations.literal: He also incited Hailing to go there. When the elite guard departed, Hailing was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged Hailing to go there. Once the elite guard had departed, Hailing was assassinated.

sentences.zh: 丙申，敵人退屯三十里，遣使議和。

translations.literal: On bingshen day the enemy withdrew thirty li and sent envoys to discuss peace.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day the enemy withdrew thirty li and sent envoys to negotiate peace.

sentences.zh: 己亥，奏聞。

translations.literal: On jihai day this was reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day Yu Yunwen reported the news to the throne.

sentences.zh: 召入對，上慰藉嘉歎，謂陳俊卿曰：「虞允文公忠出天性，朕之裴度也。」

translations.literal: He was summoned for audience. The emperor consoled and praised him in admiration, and said to Chen Junqing: "Yu Yunwen's public loyalty springs from his nature—he is my Pei Du."
translations.idiomatic: Summoned for an audience, the emperor consoled and praised him, saying to Chen Junqing, "Yu Yunwen's loyalty to the state comes from his very nature—he is my Pei Du."

sentences.zh: 詔免扈從，往兩淮措置。

translations.literal: An edict exempted him from accompanying the emperor and sent him to manage the two Huai regions.
translations.idiomatic: An edict relieved him of escort duty and dispatched him to manage affairs in the two Huai regions.

sentences.zh: 允文至鎮江，奏收兩淮三策，不報。

translations.literal: When Yunwen reached Zhenjiang, he submitted three plans for recovering the two Huai regions, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Yunwen reached Zhenjiang, he submitted three plans for recovering the two Huai regions, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，上至建康。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year the emperor reached Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year the emperor reached Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 尋議回鑾，詔以楊存中充江淮、荊襄路宣撫使，允文副之。

translations.literal: Soon the return of the imperial carriage was discussed. An edict appointed Yang Cunzhong commissioner for the Jiang-Huai and Jing-Xiang circuits, with Yunwen as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the court debated the emperor's return north. An edict appointed Yang Cunzhong commissioner for the Jiang-Huai and Jing-Xiang circuits, with Yu Yunwen as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 給、舍繳存中除命，於是允文充川陝宣諭使。

translations.literal: Drafting and remonstrance officials submitted objections to Cunzhong's appointment, and Yunwen was then appointed envoy to Sichuan and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance and drafting officials brought objections against Yang Cunzhong's appointment, and Yu Yunwen was then appointed envoy to Sichuan and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，言：「金亮既誅，新主初立，彼國方亂，天相我恢復也。

translations.literal: At his farewell audience he said: "Now that Hailing of Jin has been killed and a new ruler has just ascended, their country is in turmoil—Heaven is aiding our recovery.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience he said, "With Hailing of Jin dead and a new ruler just enthroned, their country is in chaos—Heaven is aiding our recovery.

sentences.zh: 和則海內氣沮，戰則海內氣伸。」

translations.literal: Peace would deflate the spirit within the seas; war would extend it."
translations.idiomatic: Peace would deflate the spirit of the realm; war would lift it."

sentences.zh: 上以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor considered this correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 允文至蜀，與大將吳璘議經略中原，璘進取鳳翔，復鞏州。

translations.literal: When Yunwen reached Shu, he discussed with the great general Wu Lin the strategy for managing the Central Plains. Lin advanced to take Fengxiang and recovered Gong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Yunwen reached Sichuan, he conferred with the great general Wu Lin on plans to recover the Central Plains. Wu Lin advanced on Fengxiang and retook Gong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 金治兵爭陝西新復州郡，蜀士欲棄之，允文持不可。

translations.literal: Jin mustered troops to contest the newly recovered prefectures of Shaanxi. Shu scholars wished to abandon them, but Yunwen maintained this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin mobilized forces to contest the newly recovered prefectures of Shaanxi. Sichuan officials wanted to abandon them, but Yu Yunwen insisted they must be held.

sentences.zh: 孝宗受禪，朝臣有言西事者，謂官軍進討，東不可過寶雞，北不可過德順，且欲用忠義人守新復州郡，官軍退守蜀口。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong received the abdication, court officials who spoke on western affairs said that in government troops' advance, they should not go east of Baoji or north of Deshun, and wished to use loyal volunteers to hold the newly recovered prefectures while government troops withdrew to guard the Shu passes.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaozong ascended the throne, court officials discussing western affairs argued that government forces should advance no farther east than Baoji or north than Deshun, and proposed leaving the newly recovered prefectures to loyal volunteers while regular troops fell back to guard the Sichuan passes.

sentences.zh: 允文爭之不得，吳璘遂歸河池，蓋用參知政事史浩議，欲盡棄陝西，臺諫袁季、任古附和其說。

translations.literal: Yunwen argued but could not prevail. Wu Lin then returned to Hechi. This followed the proposal of Vice Grand Councilor Shi Hao to abandon Shaanxi entirely. Remonstrance officials Yuan Ji and Ren Gu supported his view.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen argued in vain. Wu Lin then withdrew to Hechi, following Vice Grand Councilor Shi Hao's proposal to abandon Shaanxi entirely. Remonstrance officials Yuan Ji and Ren Gu endorsed his position.

sentences.zh: 允文再上疏，大略言：「恢復莫先於陝西，陝西五路新復州縣又係於德順之存亡，一旦棄之，則窺蜀之路愈多，西和、階、成，利害至重。」

translations.literal: Yunwen submitted another memorial, stating in general: "Recovery must begin with Shaanxi. The newly recovered prefectures and counties of the five Shaanxi circuits depend on whether Deshun stands or falls. Once abandoned, routes for spying on Shu would multiply. Xihe, Jie, and Cheng are of the utmost strategic importance."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen submitted another memorial, arguing in essence, "Recovery must begin with Shaanxi. The newly retaken prefectures and counties of the five Shaanxi circuits hinge on the fate of Deshun. Once we abandon them, the routes by which the enemy could probe Sichuan will multiply. Xihe, Jie, and Cheng are of the utmost strategic importance."

sentences.zh: 前後凡十五疏，且移書陳康伯，康伯牽于同列，不能回也。

translations.literal: In all he submitted fifteen memorials, and also wrote to Chen Kangbo. Kangbo, constrained by his colleagues, could not change course.
translations.idiomatic: In all he submitted fifteen memorials and also wrote to Chen Kangbo, but Kangbo, constrained by his colleagues, could not change the court's course.

sentences.zh: 上將召允文問陝西事，執政忌其來，以顯謨閣直學士知夔州，尋又命奏事。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to summon Yunwen to question him on Shaanxi affairs, but the chief ministers resented his coming and appointed him a direct academician of the Xianmo Pavilion and prefect of Kuizhou. Soon afterward he was ordered to report to court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to summon Yu Yunwen to discuss Shaanxi affairs, but the chief ministers resented his influence and appointed him direct academician of the Xianmo Pavilion and prefect of Kuizhou. Soon afterward he was ordered to report to court.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年入對，史浩既素主棄地，及拜相，亟行之，且親為詔，有曰：「棄雞肋之無多，免狼心之未已。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing he had an audience. Shi Hao had long advocated abandoning territory, and once appointed chief minister he hurried to put this into effect. He even personally drafted an edict saying: "Abandon the meager chicken ribs; spare us the wolf's heart that has not yet ceased."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longxing he had an audience. Shi Hao had long advocated abandoning territory, and once appointed chief minister he hurried to put this into effect. He even personally drafted an edict saying, "Abandon the meager chicken ribs; spare us the wolf's heart that has not yet ceased."

sentences.zh: 允文入對言：「今日有八可戰。」

translations.literal: Yunwen entered audience and said: "Today there are eight reasons we can fight."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen entered audience and said, "Today there are eight reasons we can fight."

sentences.zh: 上問及棄地，允文以笏畫地，陳其利害。

translations.literal: When the emperor asked about abandoning territory, Yunwen used his tablet to trace on the ground and explained the advantages and disadvantages.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked about abandoning territory, Yu Yunwen used his tablet to trace on the ground and explained the advantages and disadvantages.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此史浩誤朕。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Shi Hao has misled me."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Shi Hao has misled me."

sentences.zh: 以敷文閣待制知太平州，尋除兵部尚書、湖北京西宣撫使，改制置使。

translations.literal: He was appointed awaiting-draft gentleman of the Fuwen Pavilion and prefect of Taiping Prefecture. Soon afterward he was appointed minister of war and Hubei Jingxi pacification commissioner, and was changed to institutional arrangements commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed awaiting-draft gentleman of the Fuwen Pavilion and prefect of Taiping Prefecture. Soon afterward he was appointed minister of war and Hubei Jingxi pacification commissioner, and was changed to institutional arrangements commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷遣盧仲賢使金議和，湯思退又欲棄唐、鄧、海、泗，手詔謂唐、鄧非險要，可置度外，允文五上疏力爭。

translations.literal: At the time the court sent Lu Zhongxian as envoy to Jin to discuss peace. Tang Situi also wished to abandon Tang, Deng, Hai, and Si. A personal edict held that Tang and Deng were not strategically vital and could be set aside. Yunwen submitted five memorials vigorously opposing this.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court dispatched Lu Zhongxian as envoy to Jin to negotiate peace. Tang Situi also sought to abandon Tang, Deng, Hai, and Si. A personal edict declared that Tang and Deng were not strategically vital and could be set aside. Yu Yunwen submitted five memorials vigorously opposing this.

sentences.zh: 思退怒，即奏曰：「此皆以利害不切於己，大言誤國，以邀美名。

translations.literal: Situi grew angry and immediately memorialized: "These men all speak grandly to mislead the state and win a fine reputation, because the stakes do not touch them personally.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Situi grew angry and immediately memorialized, "These men speak grandly to mislead the state and win a fine reputation because the stakes do not touch them personally.

sentences.zh: 宗社大事，豈同戲劇。」

translations.literal: The great affairs of the altars of state—how can they be treated like a play?"
translations.idiomatic: The great affairs of state—how can they be treated like a play?"

sentences.zh: 上意遂定。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mind was then made up.

sentences.zh: 思退陽請召允文，實欲去之也。

translations.literal: Situi outwardly requested that Yunwen be summoned, but in fact wished to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Situi outwardly requested that Yu Yunwen be summoned, but in fact wished to remove him.

sentences.zh: 允文上印，猶以四州不可棄為請，乞致仕。

translations.literal: Yunwen returned his seal of office, yet still petitioned that the four prefectures could not be abandoned, and begged to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen returned his seal of office, yet still petitioned that the four prefectures could not be abandoned and begged to retire.

sentences.zh: 詔以顯謨閣學士知平江府。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him academician of the Xianmo Pavilion and prefect of Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him academician of the Xianmo Pavilion and prefect of Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 思退竟決和議，割唐、鄧。

translations.literal: Situi ultimately decided on a peace agreement and ceded Tang and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Situi ultimately settled on a peace agreement and ceded Tang and Deng.

sentences.zh: 二年，金兵復至，思退貶，上悔不用允文言。

translations.literal: In the second year Jin troops came again. Situi was demoted, and the emperor regretted not having heeded Yunwen's words.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Jin troops invaded again. Tang Situi was demoted, and the emperor regretted not having heeded Yu Yunwen's advice.

sentences.zh: 陳俊卿亦薦允文堪大用，除端明殿學士、同簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: Chen Junqing also recommended Yunwen as fit for great employment. He was appointed academician of the Duanming Hall and concurrent signer of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Junqing also recommended Yu Yunwen as fit for high office. He was appointed academician of the Duanming Hall and concurrent signer of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 乾道元年，拜參知政事兼知樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Qiandao reign he was appointed vice grand councilor and concurrently head of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qiandao reign he was appointed vice grand councilor and concurrently head of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 是秋，金遣完顏仲有所議，偃蹇不敬，允文請斬之，廷有異論，不果。

translations.literal: That autumn Jin sent Wanyan Zhong to discuss affairs. He was arrogant and disrespectful. Yunwen requested that he be executed, but there was dissent at court and it did not happen.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Jin sent Wanyan Zhong to negotiate. He was arrogant and disrespectful. Yu Yunwen requested that he be executed, but dissent at court prevented it.

sentences.zh: 會錢端禮受李宏玉帶，事連允文，為御史章服所論，罷政，奉祠西歸。

translations.literal: Then Qian Duanli accepted Li Hongyu's belt, and the affair implicated Yunwen. Censor Zhang Fu impeached him, and he was removed from office and sent west to serve in a temple post.
translations.idiomatic: Then Qian Duanli accepted Li Hongyu's belt, and the affair implicated Yu Yunwen. Censor Zhang Fu impeached him, and he was removed from office and sent west to serve in a temple post.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，召至闕，除知樞密院事兼參知政事。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year he was summoned to court and appointed head of the Bureau of Military Affairs and vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year he was summoned to court and appointed head of the Bureau of Military Affairs and vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 吳璘卒，議擇代，上諭允文曰：「吳璘既卒，汪應辰恐不習軍事，無以易卿。

translations.literal: When Wu Lin died, the court debated choosing a successor. The emperor told Yunwen: "Now that Wu Lin is dead, Wang Yingchen may not be skilled in military affairs—there is no one to replace you.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Lin died, the court debated choosing a successor. The emperor told Yu Yunwen, "Now that Wu Lin is dead, Wang Yingchen may not be skilled in military affairs—there is no one to replace you.

sentences.zh: 凡事不宜效張浚迂闊，軍前事，卿一一親臨之。」

translations.literal: In all affairs you must not imitate Zhang Jun's impractical grandiosity. As for affairs at the front, you must personally oversee each one."
translations.idiomatic: In all affairs you must not imitate Zhang Jun's impractical grandiosity. As for affairs at the front, you must personally oversee each one."

sentences.zh: 即拜資政殿大學士、四川宣撫使，尋詔依舊知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was then appointed grand academician of the Zizheng Hall and commissioner for Sichuan. Soon an edict ordered him to retain his post as head of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed grand academician of the Zizheng Hall and commissioner for Sichuan. Soon an edict ordered him to retain his post as head of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 歸蜀一月，召至闕，不數月復使蜀。

translations.literal: After one month back in Shu he was summoned to court. Within a few months he was sent to Shu again.
translations.idiomatic: After one month back in Sichuan he was summoned to court. Within a few months he was sent to Sichuan again.

sentences.zh: 太上賜御書《聖主得賢臣頌》，上又為之制跋，陛辭，復以所御雙履及甲胄賜焉。

translations.literal: The retired emperor bestowed the imperially written "Ode on the Sage Ruler Obtaining Worthy Ministers." The emperor also composed a colophon for it. At his farewell audience he was again given the emperor's own pair of shoes and armor.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor bestowed the imperially written "Ode on the Sage Ruler Obtaining Worthy Ministers." The emperor also composed a colophon for it. At his farewell audience he was again given the emperor's own pair of shoes and a suit of armor.

sentences.zh: 過郢，奏築黃鷹山城。

translations.literal: Passing through Ying, he memorialized on building Huangying Mountain Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Ying, he memorialized on building Huangying Mountain Fort.

sentences.zh: 過襄陽，奏修府城。

translations.literal: Passing through Xiangyang, he memorialized on repairing the prefectural walls.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Xiangyang, he memorialized on repairing the prefectural walls.

sentences.zh: 八月至漢中，又往沔陽。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he reached Hanzhong, then went on to Mianyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he reached Hanzhong, then went on to Mianyang.

sentences.zh: 九月，至益昌。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he reached Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he reached Yichang.

sentences.zh: 先被手詔戒九事，洎至蜀，悉奉而行，尤以軍政為急。

translations.literal: He had first received a personal edict warning him on nine matters. When he reached Shu he carried them all out, taking military administration as especially urgent.
translations.idiomatic: He had first received a personal edict warning him on nine matters. When he reached Sichuan he carried them all out, treating military administration as especially urgent.

sentences.zh: 又奏閱實諸軍，第其壯怯為三，上備戰，中下備輜重，老者少者不預。

translations.literal: He also memorialized on inspecting all armies, ranking them by strength and weakness into three grades: the top prepared for battle, the middle and lower for baggage, while the old and young were excluded.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized on inspecting all armies, ranking them by strength and weakness into three grades: the top tier prepared for battle, the middle and lower for baggage, while the old and young were excluded.

sentences.zh: 汰兵凡萬人，減緡錢四百萬。

translations.literal: In all ten thousand troops were cut, saving four million strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: In all ten thousand troops were cut, saving four million strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 汰去兵有勞績者，置員闕處之。

translations.literal: Soldiers cut from the rolls who had records of merit were placed in vacant posts.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers cut from the rolls who had records of merit were placed in vacant posts.

sentences.zh: 興、洋義士，民兵也，紹興初以七萬計，大散之戰，將不授甲，驅之先官軍，死亡略盡。

translations.literal: Righteous volunteers of Xing and Yang were militia. At the beginning of the Shaoxing reign they numbered seventy thousand. At the battle of Dasan, the generals did not issue armor but drove them ahead of the regular army, and they were nearly all killed.
translations.idiomatic: The righteous volunteers of Xing and Yang were militia. At the beginning of the Shaoxing reign they numbered seventy thousand. At the battle of Dasan, the generals did not issue them armor but drove them ahead of the regular army, and they were nearly all killed.

sentences.zh: 命利帥晁公武核實，得二萬三千九百餘人。

translations.literal: He ordered the Li circuit intendant Chao Gongwu to verify the rolls and found twenty-three thousand nine hundred and more men.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Li circuit intendant Chao Gongwu to verify the rolls and found twenty-three thousand nine hundred and more men.

sentences.zh: 又得陝西弓箭手法，參紹興制為一書，俾將吏守之。

translations.literal: He also obtained the Shaanxi archery technique, combined it with the Shaoxing regulations into one book, and had commanders and officials observe it.
translations.idiomatic: He also obtained the Shaanxi archery technique, combined it with the Shaoxing regulations into one manual, and had commanders and officials observe it.

sentences.zh: 以馬政付張松，奏依舊制分茶馬為川、秦司。

translations.literal: He entrusted horse administration to Zhang Song and memorialized on restoring the old system of dividing tea-and-horse affairs into Sichuan and Shaanxi offices.
translations.idiomatic: He entrusted horse administration to Zhang Song and memorialized on restoring the old system of dividing tea-and-horse affairs into Sichuan and Shaanxi offices.

sentences.zh: 初在樞府，蕭遮巴以刷軍中人為言，允文嘗奏諭三衙撫存之。

translations.literal: When he was first in the Bureau of Military Affairs, Xiao Zheba spoke on behalf of men purged from the armies. Yunwen had once memorialized instructing the three palace commands to care for them.
translations.idiomatic: When he was first in the Bureau of Military Affairs, Xiao Zheba spoke on behalf of men purged from the armies. Yu Yunwen had once memorialized instructing the three palace commands to care for them.

sentences.zh: 至是，金、洋、興元歸正人二萬，遮道訴繫縲之苦，允文分給官田，俾咸振業。

translations.literal: At this time twenty thousand men who had returned to allegiance from Jin, Yang, and Xingyuan blocked the road complaining of the hardship of imprisonment. Yunwen allotted them official fields so that all could revive their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: At this time twenty thousand men who had returned to allegiance from Jin, Yang, and Xingyuan blocked the road complaining of the hardship of imprisonment. Yu Yunwen allotted them official fields so that all could revive their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 欲結敵將姜挺、白沂，遵御劄募鞏人王嗣祖結外蕃以圖金人，又得蕃僧六彪者偕往，竟無成說。

translations.literal: He wished to win over the enemy generals Jiang Ting and Bai Yi. Following an imperial note he recruited Wang Sizu of Gong to win over outer tribes against the Jurchens, and also obtained the Tibetan monk Liu Biao to go with him, but in the end nothing came of it.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to win over the enemy generals Jiang Ting and Bai Yi. Following an imperial note he recruited Wang Sizu of Gong to win over outer tribes against the Jurchens, and also obtained the Tibetan monk Liu Biao to go with him, but in the end nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 時邛、蜀十四郡告饑，荒政凡六十五事，劍倅獻羨錢五萬，卻之。

translations.literal: At the time fourteen prefectures of Qiong and Shu reported famine. Relief measures totaled sixty-five items. The sword prefectural aide offered surplus funds of fifty thousand, which he declined.
translations.idiomatic: At the time fourteen prefectures of Qiong and Shu reported famine. Relief measures totaled sixty-five items. The sword prefectural aide offered surplus funds of fifty thousand, which he declined.

sentences.zh: 五年八月，拜右僕射、同中書門下平章事兼樞密使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifth year he was appointed right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrent grand councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and commissioner of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fifth year he was appointed right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrent grand councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 允文多薦知名士，如洪适、汪應辰。

translations.literal: Yunwen often recommended well-known scholars such as Hong Kuo and Wang Yingchen.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen often recommended well-known scholars such as Hong Kuo and Wang Yingchen.

sentences.zh: 及為相，籍人才為三等，有所見聞即記之，號《材館錄》。

translations.literal: When he became chief minister he catalogued talent in three grades. Whatever he saw or heard he recorded in a work called "Records of the Talent Hall."
translations.idiomatic: When he became chief minister he catalogued talent in three grades. Whatever he saw or heard he recorded in a work called "Records of the Talent Hall."

sentences.zh: 凡所舉，上皆收用，如胡銓、周必大、王十朋、趙汝愚、晁公武、李燾其尤章明者也。

translations.literal: All whom he recommended the emperor employed, such as Hu Quan, Zhou Bida, Wang Shipeng, Zhao Ruyu, Chao Gongwu, and Li Tao—these were especially notable.
translations.idiomatic: All whom he recommended the emperor employed, such as Hu Quan, Zhou Bida, Wang Shipeng, Zhao Ruyu, Chao Gongwu, and Li Tao—these were especially notable.

sentences.zh: 上以兵冗財匱為憂，允文與陳俊卿議革三衙雜役，汰冗籍，三軍無怨言。

translations.literal: The emperor worried about redundant troops and depleted finances. Yunwen and Chen Junqing discussed reforming miscellaneous corvée in the three palace commands and cutting redundant rolls. The three armies had no complaints.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor worried about redundant troops and depleted finances. Yu Yunwen and Chen Junqing discussed reforming miscellaneous corvée in the three palace commands and cutting redundant rolls. The three armies had no complaints.

sentences.zh: 口六年，陳俊卿以奏留龔茂良忤上意，上震怒甚，俊卿待命浙江亭，兩日不報。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Chen Junqing offended the emperor by memorializing to retain Gong Maoliang. The emperor was greatly enraged. Junqing awaited orders at Zhejiang Pavilion for two days without response.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Chen Junqing offended the emperor by memorializing to retain Gong Maoliang. The emperor was greatly enraged. Junqing awaited orders at Zhejiang Pavilion for two days without response.

sentences.zh: 允文請對，極論體貌之道，疊拜榻前，遂命判福州。

translations.literal: Yunwen requested an audience and spoke exhaustively on the way to treat a minister's dignity. Bowing repeatedly before the couch, he then received orders appointing Junqing judge of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen requested an audience and spoke exhaustively on the proper way to treat a minister's dignity. Bowing repeatedly before the imperial couch, he secured an order appointing Junqing judge of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔以范成大為祈請使，為陵寢故。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Fan Chengda envoy to offer prayers, on account of the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Fan Chengda envoy to offer prayers on account of the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 金不從，且諜報欲以三十萬騎奉遷陵寢來歸，中外洶洶，荊、襄將帥皆請增戍。

translations.literal: Jin did not agree, and spies reported that they wished to send three hundred thousand horsemen to escort the tombs back in relocation. Inside and outside the court there was uproar, and generals of Jing and Xiang all requested increased garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Jin did not agree, and spies reported that they wished to send three hundred thousand horsemen to escort the tombs back in relocation. Inside and outside the court there was uproar, and generals of Jing and Xiang all requested increased garrisons.

sentences.zh: 允文謂：「金方懲亮，決不輕動，不過以虛聲撼我耳。」

translations.literal: Yunwen said: "Jin has just punished Hailing and will certainly not move lightly. This is nothing but an empty threat to shake us."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen said, "Jin has just punished Hailing and will certainly not move lightly. This is nothing but an empty threat to shake us."

sentences.zh: 遂奏止之。

translations.literal: He then memorialized to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized to stop it.

sentences.zh: 朝論紛然，允文屹不動，敵卒無他。

translations.literal: Court opinion was divided, but Yunwen stood firm unmoved. The enemy in the end did nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion was divided, but Yu Yunwen stood firm unmoved. The enemy in the end did nothing else.

sentences.zh: 自莊文太子斃，儲位未定。

translations.literal: Since Crown Prince Zhuangwen died, the succession was unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Since Crown Prince Zhuangwen died, the succession was unsettled.

sentences.zh: 允文上疏，且屢懇陳。

translations.literal: Yunwen submitted a memorial and repeatedly pleaded earnestly.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen submitted a memorial and repeatedly pleaded earnestly.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，上兩宮尊號，議始定，下詔皇第三子恭王惇立為皇太子，皇子愷以雄武、保寧軍節度使判寧國府。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year the emperor bestowed honorific titles on the two palaces. The debate was then settled. An edict was issued establishing the emperor's third son, Prince Gong Dun, as crown prince. Prince Kai was made military commissioner of Xiongwu and Baoning and judge of Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year the emperor bestowed honorific titles on the two palaces. The debate was then settled. An edict established the emperor's third son, Prince Gong Dun, as crown prince. Prince Kai was made military commissioner of Xiongwu and Baoning and judge of Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 皇太子尋尹臨安。

translations.literal: The crown prince soon served as governor of Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince soon served as governor of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 侍衛馬軍司牧地舊在臨安，允文謂地狹不利芻牧，請令就牧鎮江，緩急用騎過江便。

translations.literal: The pasture lands of the Palace Horse Army Command had formerly been at Lin'an. Yunwen said the land was narrow and unfavorable for grazing, and requested that horses be pastured at Zhenjiang instead, so that in an emergency cavalry could cross the river conveniently.
translations.idiomatic: The pasture lands of the Palace Horse Army Command had formerly been at Lin'an. Yu Yunwen said the land was too narrow for grazing and requested that horses be pastured at Zhenjiang instead, so that in an emergency cavalry could cross the river conveniently.

sentences.zh: 三軍有怨語，其後言者以此為言。

translations.literal: The three armies had resentful talk, and later critics used this against him.
translations.idiomatic: The three armies grumbled, and later critics used this against him.

sentences.zh: 胡銓以臺評去，允文奏留之經筵。

translations.literal: Hu Quan left on account of a censorial review. Yunwen memorialized to retain him at the imperial lecture hall.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Quan left on account of a censorial review. Yu Yunwen memorialized to retain him at the imperial lecture hall.

sentences.zh: 銓薦朱熹，上問允文識熹否？

translations.literal: Quan recommended Zhu Xi. The emperor asked Yunwen whether he knew Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Quan recommended Zhu Xi. The emperor asked Yu Yunwen whether he knew Xi.

sentences.zh: 允文謂熹不在程頤下，遂召熹，熹不至。

translations.literal: Yunwen said Xi was not beneath Cheng Yi. Xi was then summoned, but Xi did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen said Xi was not beneath Cheng Yi. Zhu Xi was then summoned, but he did not come.

sentences.zh: 檢鼓院以六條抑上書人，允文力言不可，從之。

translations.literal: The Inspection and Remonstrance Office used six articles to suppress those who submitted memorials. Yunwen strongly argued this could not be done, and the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The Inspection and Remonstrance Office used six articles to suppress those who submitted memorials. Yu Yunwen strongly argued this could not be done, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 會慶節，金使烏林答天錫入見，金主婿也，驕倨甚，固請上降榻問金主起居，上不許，天錫跪不起，侍臣錯愕失措。

translations.literal: At the celebration of the imperial birthday, the Jin envoy Wulindati entered audience. He was the Jin ruler's son-in-law and was extremely arrogant and insolent. He insisted that the emperor descend from the throne to inquire after the Jin ruler's health. The emperor refused. Wulindati knelt and would not rise. Attending officials were startled and at a loss.
translations.idiomatic: At the celebration of the imperial birthday, the Jin envoy Wulindati entered audience. He was the Jin ruler's son-in-law and was extremely arrogant and insolent. He insisted that the emperor descend from the throne to inquire after the Jin ruler's health. The emperor refused. Wulindati knelt and would not rise. Attending officials were startled and at a loss.

sentences.zh: 允文請大駕還禁中，且諭之曰：「大駕既興，難再御殿，使人來且隨班上壽。」

translations.literal: Yunwen requested that the imperial carriage return to the inner palace, and also instructed him: "Once the imperial carriage has risen, it is hard to mount the hall again. When the envoy comes, let him follow the court ranks to offer birthday congratulations."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen requested that the imperial carriage return to the inner palace, and also instructed him, "Once the imperial carriage has risen, it is hard to mount the hall again. When the envoy comes, let him follow the court ranks to offer birthday congratulations."

sentences.zh: 金使慚而退。

translations.literal: The Jin envoy withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin envoy withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 上以僕射名不正，改為左、右丞相。

translations.literal: The emperor considered the title of vice director incorrect and changed it to left and right chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor considered the title of vice director incorrect and changed it to left and right chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 八年二月，授允文特進、左丞相兼樞密使，梁克家為右丞相。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year Yunwen was appointed special advance and left chief minister and commissioner of military affairs. Liang Kejia was made right chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighth year Yu Yunwen was appointed special advance and left chief minister and commissioner of military affairs. Liang Kejia was made right chief minister.

sentences.zh: 允文嘗舉克家自代，上不許。

translations.literal: Yunwen had once recommended Kejia to succeed him. The emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen had once recommended Liang Kejia to succeed him. The emperor did not agree.

sentences.zh: 是月，以病乞解機政，又薦克家靖重有宰相器，至是始同相，手詔付允文曰：「朕方欲武臣為樞密，曹勛如何？」

translations.literal: That month, citing illness he requested release from state affairs and again recommended Kejia as steady and possessed of the capacity of a chief minister. Only then did they serve together as chief ministers. A personal edict was given to Yunwen: "I am just now wishing for a military man as head of the Bureau of Military Affairs. What of Cao Xun?"
translations.idiomatic: That month, citing illness he requested release from state affairs and again recommended Liang Kejia as steady and possessed of the capacity of a chief minister. Only then did they serve together as chief ministers. A personal edict was given to Yu Yunwen, "I am just now wishing for a military man as head of the Bureau of Military Affairs. What of Cao Xun?"

sentences.zh: 允文謂勛人品卑凡，不可用。

translations.literal: Yunwen said Xun's character was base and common and he could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen said Cao Xun's character was base and common and he could not be used.

sentences.zh: 既而以張說簽書樞密院事，右正言王希呂與臺官交劾之。

translations.literal: Then Zhang Shuo was appointed signer of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Right remonstrance official Wang Xilü and censorial officials jointly impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Then Zhang Shuo was appointed signer of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Right remonstrance official Wang Xilü and censorial officials jointly impeached him.

sentences.zh: 上怒希呂甚，手詔「與遠惡監當」，允文繳回，上益怒。

translations.literal: The emperor was very angry with Xilü. A personal edict ordered "remote harsh supervisory assignment." Yunwen returned it with an objection. The emperor grew angrier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was very angry with Wang Xilü. A personal edict ordered "remote harsh supervisory assignment." Yu Yunwen returned it with an objection. The emperor grew angrier.

sentences.zh: 梁克家曰：「希呂論張說，臺綱也，左相救希呂，國體也。」

translations.literal: Liang Kejia said: "Xilü impeached Zhang Shuo—that is the censorial standard. The left chief minister saving Xilü—that is the dignity of the state."
translations.idiomatic: Liang Kejia said, "Wang Xilü impeached Zhang Shuo—that is the censorial standard. The left chief minister saving Xilü—that is the dignity of the state."

sentences.zh: 上怒稍解，卒薄希呂之罰。

translations.literal: The emperor's anger eased slightly, and in the end Xilü's punishment was lightened.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger eased slightly, and in the end Wang Xilü's punishment was lightened.

sentences.zh: 四月，御史蕭之敏劾允文，允文上章待罪。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Censor Xiao Zhimin impeached Yunwen. Yunwen submitted a memorial awaiting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Censor Xiao Zhimin impeached Yu Yunwen. Yu Yunwen submitted a memorial awaiting punishment.

sentences.zh: 上過德壽宮，太上曰：「采石之功，之敏在何許？

translations.literal: The emperor visited the Virtue and Longevity Palace. The retired emperor said: "At the merit of Caishi, where was Zhimin?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited the Virtue and Longevity Palace. The retired emperor said, "At the merit of Caishi, where was Zhimin?

sentences.zh: 毋聽其去。」

translations.literal: Do not listen to his request to leave."
translations.idiomatic: Do not listen to his request to leave."

sentences.zh: 上為出之敏，且書扇制詩以留之。

translations.literal: The emperor removed Zhimin on his behalf and also wrote an inscribed poem on a fan to keep him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor removed Xiao Zhimin on Yu Yunwen's behalf and also wrote an inscribed poem on a fan to keep him.

sentences.zh: 允文言之敏端方，請召歸以辟言路。

translations.literal: Yunwen said Zhimin was upright and requested that he be recalled to open the path of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen said Xiao Zhimin was upright and requested that he be recalled to open the path of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 上謂其言寬厚，命曾懷書之《時政記》。

translations.literal: The emperor said his words were generous and ordered Zeng Huai to record them in the "Record of Current Policy."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said his words were generous and ordered Zeng Huai to record them in the "Record of Current Policy."

sentences.zh: 上命選諫官，允文以李彥潁、林光朝、王質對，三人皆鯁亮，又以文學推重于時，故薦之，久不報。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the selection of remonstrance officials. Yunwen answered with Li Yanying, Lin Guangchao, and Wang Zhi. All three were blunt and bright, and he also recommended them for their literary learning, which was respected at the time. For a long time there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the selection of remonstrance officials. Yu Yunwen named Li Yanying, Lin Guangchao, and Wang Zhi. All three were blunt and bright, and he also recommended them for their literary learning, which was respected at the time. For a long time there was no response.

sentences.zh: 曾覿薦一人，賜第，擢諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Zeng Di recommended one man, granted him a mansion, and promoted him to remonstrance grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Di recommended one man, granted him a mansion, and promoted him to remonstrance grandee.

sentences.zh: 允文、克家爭之，不從。

translations.literal: Yunwen and Kejia contested this, but the emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen and Liang Kejia contested this, but the emperor did not agree.

sentences.zh: 允文力求去，授少保、武安軍節度使、四川宣撫使，進封雍國公。

translations.literal: Yunwen vigorously sought to leave. He was appointed junior guardian, military commissioner of the Wu'an Army, and commissioner for Sichuan, and was advanced in rank to Duke of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen vigorously sought to leave. He was appointed junior guardian, military commissioner of the Wu'an Army, and commissioner for Sichuan, and was advanced in rank to Duke of Yong.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，上諭以進取之方，期以某日會河南。

translations.literal: At his farewell audience the emperor instructed him on the method of advance, fixing a day on which they would meet south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience the emperor instructed him on the method of advance, fixing a day on which they would meet south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 允文言：「異時戒內外不相應。」

translations.literal: Yunwen said: "In the past the warning was that inner and outer would not coordinate."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen said, "In the past the warning was that inner and outer would not coordinate."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「若西師出而朕遲回，即朕負卿；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If the western army goes out and I hesitate, then I have failed you;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If the western army goes out and I hesitate, then I have failed you;

sentences.zh: 若朕已動而卿遲回，即卿負朕。」

translations.literal: If I have already moved and you hesitate, then you have failed me."
translations.idiomatic: If I have already moved and you hesitate, then you have failed me."

sentences.zh: 上御正衙，酌酒賦詩以遣之，且賜家廟祭器。

translations.literal: The emperor mounted the main hall, poured wine, composed a poem, and sent him off, also bestowing ancestral temple ritual vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mounted the main hall, poured wine, composed a poem, and sent him off, also bestowing ancestral temple ritual vessels.

sentences.zh: 九年至蜀。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he reached Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he reached Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 大軍月給米一石五斗，不足贍其家，允文捐宣司錢三十萬易米，計口增給。

translations.literal: The great army's monthly ration was one picul and five dou of rice, insufficient to support their families. Yunwen contributed three hundred thousand of the commissioner's funds to exchange for rice and increased the ration by head count.
translations.idiomatic: The great army's monthly ration was one picul and five dou of rice, insufficient to support their families. Yu Yunwen contributed three hundred thousand of the commissioner's funds to exchange for rice and increased the ration by head count.

sentences.zh: 立戶馬七條，括民馬，奏選良家子以儲戰用。

translations.literal: He established seven articles on household horses, registered private horses, and memorialized on selecting sons of good families to store up for military use.
translations.idiomatic: He established seven articles on household horses, registered private horses, and memorialized on selecting sons of good families to store up for military use.

sentences.zh: 初，北界有寇鄰者，擁眾數萬在商、虢間，允文秉政日納款，迨至蜀，復遣人致書允文，不報，羈縻之而已。

translations.literal: At first on the northern border there was a bandit chief named Lin who gathered a host of tens of thousands between Shang and Guo. During Yunwen's time in office he submitted allegiance. When Yunwen reached Shu, he again sent men with a letter to Yunwen, who did not reply but merely kept him in loose restraint.
translations.idiomatic: At first on the northern border there was a bandit chief named Lin who gathered a host of tens of thousands between Shang and Guo. During Yu Yunwen's time in office he submitted allegiance. When Yu Yunwen reached Sichuan, Lin again sent men with a letter to him, but Yu Yunwen did not reply and merely kept him in loose restraint.

sentences.zh: 既而鄰謀覺，金密遣人捕之。

translations.literal: Soon Lin's plot was discovered. Jin secretly sent men to capture him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lin's plot was discovered. Jin secretly sent men to capture him.

sentences.zh: 葉衡奏聞，允文上疏自辨，因請納祿，不報。

translations.literal: Ye Heng reported this to the throne. Yunwen submitted a memorial in self-defense and therefore requested to surrender his salary. He received no response.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Heng reported this to the throne. Yu Yunwen submitted a memorial in self-defense and therefore requested to surrender his salary. He received no response.

sentences.zh: 上嘗謂允文曰：「丙午之恥，當與丞相共雪之。」

translations.literal: The emperor once said to Yunwen: "The shame of bingwu must be washed away together with the chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said to Yu Yunwen, "The shame of bingwu must be washed away together with the chief minister."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「朕惟功業不如唐太宗，富庶不如漢文、景。」

translations.literal: He also said: "My achievements alone do not match those of Emperor Taizong of Tang, and my wealth and prosperity do not match those of Emperors Wen and Jing of Han."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "My achievements alone do not match those of Emperor Taizong of Tang, and my wealth and prosperity do not match those of Emperors Wen and Jing of Han."

sentences.zh: 故允文許上以恢復。

translations.literal: Therefore Yunwen promised the emperor recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Yu Yunwen promised the emperor recovery.

sentences.zh: 使蜀一歲，無進兵期，上賜密詔趣之，允文言軍需未備，上不樂。

translations.literal: After a year in Shu with no timetable for advancing troops, the emperor sent a secret edict urging him on. Yunwen said military supplies were not ready, and the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: After serving in Shu for a year with no plan to advance, the emperor sent a secret edict pressing him to act. Yu Yunwen replied that military supplies were not ready, and the emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 淳熙元年薨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of the Chunxi era.

sentences.zh: 後四年，上幸白石大閱，見軍皆少壯，謂輔臣曰：「虞允文行沙汰之效也。」

translations.literal: Four years later, the emperor reviewed troops at Baishi and saw that the army was all young and strong. He said to his chief ministers: "This is the effect of Yu Yunwen's weeding out.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later, the emperor reviewed troops at Baishi and saw an army of young, vigorous men. He told his chief ministers, "This is the effect of Yu Yunwen's winnowing of the ranks."

sentences.zh: 尋詔贈太傅，賜諡「忠肅」。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter an edict posthumously granted him Grand Tutor and bestowed the posthumous title "Loyal and Solemn."
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward an edict posthumously made him Grand Tutor and granted the posthumous title "Loyal and Solemn."

sentences.zh: 允文姿雄偉，長六尺四寸，慷慨磊落有大志，而言動有則度，人望而知為任重之器。

translations.literal: Yunwen was imposing in bearing, six feet four inches tall, magnanimous and upright with great ambitions. His words and conduct had proper measure; at a glance people knew he was one capable of bearing heavy responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen was imposing in bearing, six feet four inches tall, open-hearted and upright with lofty ambitions. His words and deeds were measured; at a glance people knew he was fit for weighty responsibility.

sentences.zh: 早以文學致身臺閣，晚際時艱，出入將相垂二十年，孜孜忠勤無二焉。

translations.literal: Early he rose to the halls of office through literary learning; late he encountered national crisis, moving between general and minister for nearly twenty years, diligently loyal without wavering.
translations.idiomatic: Early he reached the halls of office through literary accomplishment; late he met national crisis and moved between general and minister for nearly twenty years, tirelessly loyal without deviation.

sentences.zh: 嘗注《唐書》、《五代史》，藏於家。

translations.literal: He once annotated the History of Tang and History of the Five Dynasties, keeping them at home.
translations.idiomatic: He once annotated the History of Tang and the History of the Five Dynasties, keeping the manuscripts at home.

sentences.zh: 有詩文十卷，《經筵春秋講義》三卷，《奏議》二十二卷，《內外志》十五卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He had ten juan of poetry and prose, three juan of Lectures on the Spring and Autumn Annals for the Classic Mat, twenty-two juan of Memorials and Proposals, and fifteen juan of Internal and External Affairs, all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His works included ten juan of poetry and prose, three juan of Lectures on the Spring and Autumn Annals for the Classic Mat, twenty-two juan of Memorials and Proposals, and fifteen juan of Internal and External Affairs — all in circulation.

sentences.zh: 子三人：公亮、公著、杭孫。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Gongliang, Gongzhu, and Hang.
translations.idiomatic: His three sons were Gongliang, Gongzhu, and Hang.

sentences.zh: 孫八人，皆好修，唯剛簡最知名，嘉定中，召不至，終利路提點刑獄。

translations.literal: He had eight grandsons, all devoted to self-cultivation; Gangjian alone was most renowned. During the Jiading era he was summoned but did not come, and ended as judicial intendant of Lizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He had eight grandsons, all devoted to self-cultivation; Gangjian alone was most renowned. During the Jiading era he was summoned but did not come, and ended his career as judicial intendant of Lizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 辛次膺

translations.literal: Xin Ciying
translations.idiomatic: Xin Ciying.

sentences.zh: 辛次膺，字起季，萊州人。

translations.literal: Xin Ciying, courtesy name Qiji, was a native of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Ciying, styled Qiji, was from Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，從母依外氏王聖美於丹徒。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he followed his mother to live with her maternal clan, Wang Shengmei, at Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he followed his mother to live with her maternal relatives, the Wang family of Shengmei, at Dantu.

sentences.zh: 俊慧力學，日誦千言。

translations.literal: Clever and gifted, he studied diligently and could recite a thousand words per day.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and gifted, he applied himself to learning and could recite a thousand words each day.

sentences.zh: 甫冠，登政和二年進士第，歷官為單父丞。

translations.literal: Just after coming of age he passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Zhenghe, and served successively as assistant magistrate of Shanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after coming of age he passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Zhenghe and served as assistant magistrate of Shanfu.

sentences.zh: 值山東亂，舉室南渡。

translations.literal: When Shandong fell into turmoil, his whole household fled south.
translations.idiomatic: When Shandong fell into turmoil, his entire household fled south.

sentences.zh: 屬閩寇范汝為陷建州，宰相呂頤浩以次膺宰浦城，遏賊衝。

translations.literal: When the Fujian bandit Fan Ruwei seized Jianzhou, Grand Councilor Lu Yihao appointed Ciying magistrate of Pucheng to block the bandits' advance.
translations.idiomatic: When the Fujian bandit Fan Ruwei seized Jianzhou, Grand Councilor Lu Yihao appointed Ciying magistrate of Pucheng to block the bandits' line of attack.

sentences.zh: 比至，寇黨熊志寧已焚其邑。

translations.literal: By the time he arrived, the bandit follower Xiong Zhining had already burned the town.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived, the bandit follower Xiong Zhining had already burned the county seat.

sentences.zh: 於是披荊棘，坐瓦礫中，安輯吏民，料丁壯，治器械，厄險阻，號令不煩，邑民便之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he cleared thorns, sat amid the rubble, settled officials and people, counted able-bodied men, prepared weapons, held strategic passes, and issued orders without harassment — the townspeople found this convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he cleared thorns, sat amid the rubble, settled officials and commoners, counted able-bodied men, prepared weapons, held strategic passes, and issued orders without vexation — the townspeople welcomed this.

sentences.zh: 數月，韓世忠破賊，復建州，除審計司。

translations.literal: Within months Han Shizhong defeated the bandits and recovered Jianzhou. Ciying was appointed to the Audit Office.
translations.idiomatic: Within months Han Shizhong defeated the bandits and recovered Jianzhou, and Ciying was appointed to the Audit Office.

sentences.zh: 餘黨范黑龍破鄰邑，閩帥張守檄次膺，俟賊平而後行。

translations.literal: Remnant bandits under Fan Heilong ravaged neighboring counties. Fujian commander Zhang Shou ordered Ciying to wait until the bandits were suppressed before departing.
translations.idiomatic: Remnant bandits under Fan Heilong ravaged neighboring counties. Fujian commander Zhang Shou ordered Ciying to wait until the bandits were pacified before departing.

sentences.zh: 乃募鄉兵習強弩，賊至，與之夾水而陣，矢齊發，賊奔潰，生致首領五人，餘悉宥之。

translations.literal: He recruited local militia to train with powerful crossbows. When the bandits came, he drew up battle lines facing them across the water, arrows flying together; the bandits fled in rout. He captured five leaders alive and pardoned the rest.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited local militia to train with powerful crossbows. When the bandits arrived, he drew up lines facing them across the water and loosed a volley together; the bandits broke and fled. He captured five leaders alive and pardoned the rest.

sentences.zh: 用參政孟庾薦，召對，奏用人貴于務實，施令在於必行。

translations.literal: On Vice Grand Councilor Meng Yu's recommendation he was summoned for audience and memorialized that employing men should value practicality and issuing orders must mean enforcement.
translations.idiomatic: On Vice Grand Councilor Meng Yu's recommendation he was summoned for audience and argued that appointing men should value practical results and issuing orders must mean certain enforcement.

sentences.zh: 遷駕部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Transport Department.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Transport Bureau.

sentences.zh: 願敕郡邑省耕薄征，務農抑末。

translations.literal: He asked that the emperor instruct prefectures and counties to reduce cultivation levies and lighten taxation, promote agriculture and restrain commerce.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the emperor instruct prefectures and counties to ease farming burdens and lighten levies, promote agriculture and restrain commerce.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「中原之人，棄墳墓生業，從巡江左，饑寒殞仆。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "People of the Central Plains have abandoned ancestral graves and livelihoods to follow the court east of the Yangtze; hungry and cold, they collapse and die.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized, "People of the Central Plains have abandoned ancestral graves and livelihoods to follow the court south of the Yangtze; hungry and cold, they collapse and die.

sentences.zh: 願加存拊，可以堅中原徯后之心。」

translations.literal: I ask that relief and care be increased — this can strengthen the hearts of those in the Central Plains who await the sovereign's return.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that relief and care be increased — this can strengthen the hearts of those in the Central Plains who await the sovereign's return."

sentences.zh: 遷吏部郎、湖北運判，中途召還，見高宗于建康行宮，首言救世之弊，上稱善，敕以所奏榜朝堂。

translations.literal: He was promoted to a post in the Ministry of Personnel and made transport commissioner for Hubei, but was recalled midway. He saw Emperor Gaozong at the temporary palace in Jiankang and first spoke of the ills afflicting the realm. The emperor praised him and ordered his memorial posted in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted within the Ministry of Personnel and appointed transport commissioner for Hubei, but was recalled en route. At the temporary palace in Jiankang he saw Emperor Gaozong and opened with the ills afflicting the realm. The emperor praised him and ordered his memorial posted in the court hall.

sentences.zh: 擢右正言。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Remonstrance Official of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Remonstrance Official.

sentences.zh: 奏：「願閱兵將，親簡拔，攬恩威之柄，使人人知朝廷之尊。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "I wish that military commanders be reviewed and personally selected, that the handles of favor and severity be grasped, so that all may know the dignity of the court.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "I wish that military commanders be reviewed and personally selected, that the handles of favor and severity be grasped, so that all may know the dignity of the court.

sentences.zh: 左右近習，久則干政，願杜其漸。

translations.literal: Those close at hand, over time, meddle in government — I ask that this tendency be stopped at its start.
translations.idiomatic: Those close at hand, over time, meddle in government — I ask that this tendency be stopped at its start.

sentences.zh: 兵連不解，十年於茲。

translations.literal: War has continued unbroken for ten years now.
translations.idiomatic: War has continued unbroken for ten years now.

sentences.zh: 一歲用錢三十萬、米四百萬石，諸路常賦僅足支其半，餘悉取諸民。

translations.literal: Each year thirty million strings of cash and four million shi of grain are consumed; regular levies from all circuits barely cover half — the rest is entirely extracted from the people.
translations.idiomatic: Each year thirty million strings of cash and four million shi of grain are consumed; regular levies from all circuits barely cover half — the rest is entirely extracted from the people.

sentences.zh: 乞罷不急之務，節姑息之澤，省冗官，汰愞兵。」

translations.literal: I beg that non-urgent affairs be suspended, indulgent largesse be curtailed, superfluous officials be reduced, and cowardly troops be weeded out.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that non-urgent affairs be suspended, indulgent largesse be curtailed, superfluous officials be reduced, and cowardly troops be weeded out."

sentences.zh: 韓世忠男直秘閣，次膺奏曰：「攻城野戰，世忠功也，其子何與？

translations.literal: When Han Shizhong's son was appointed to the Imperial Archives, Ciying memorialized: "Storming cities and fighting in the field — that was Shizhong's merit. What has his son to do with it?
translations.idiomatic: When Han Shizhong's son was appointed to the Imperial Archives, Ciying memorialized, "Storming cities and fighting in the field — that was Shizhong's merit. What has his son to do with it?

sentences.zh: 石渠、東觀，圖書府也，武功何與？

translations.literal: The Stone Canal and Eastern Pavilion are repositories of books — what has military achievement to do with them?
translations.idiomatic: The Stone Canal and Eastern Pavilion are repositories of books — what has military achievement to do with them?

sentences.zh: 幸門一啟，援例者眾。」

translations.literal: Once the gate of favor is opened, those citing precedent will be many.
translations.idiomatic: Once the gate of favor is opened, those citing precedent will be many."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「今主議者見小利忽大計，偏師偶勝，遽思進討，便謂攻為有餘；

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Those directing policy today seize on small gains and neglect the grand design. When a detached force wins by chance, they eagerly plan an advance and declare offense more than sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized, "Those directing policy today seize on small gains and neglect the grand design. When a detached force wins by chance, they eagerly plan an advance and declare offense more than sufficient.

sentences.zh: 警奏稍聞，首陳退舍，便謂守為不足。

translations.literal: When warning reports are barely heard, they put retreat first and declare defense insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: When warning reports are barely heard, they put retreat first and declare defense insufficient.

sentences.zh: 願嚴紀律，謹烽燧，明間探。」

translations.literal: I ask that discipline be tightened, beacon-fires maintained with care, and scouting made clear.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that discipline be tightened, beacon-fires maintained with care, and scouting made clear."

sentences.zh: 上皆信納。

translations.literal: The emperor trusted and accepted all of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor trusted and accepted all of it.

sentences.zh: 聞韓世忠將自楚州移軍鎮江，復陳可慮者五。

translations.literal: Learning that Han Shizhong would move his army from Chuzhou to Zhenjiang, he again set forth five points of concern.
